## 2026.8.0 (August 2026)

### Minor Changes

- #2078 `18613f7` Thanks @sprasoon_sfemu! - Add OMS shipment tracking to the Order Details page. When an order has Salesforce Order Management tracking data, each shipment shows the tracking number as a link to the carrier's tracking page, the carrier name, and the expected and actual delivery dates; a "Track shipment" action links straight to the carrier (or to the tracking section when no carrier link is available). Orders without OMS data continue to show the existing tracking number and status. The Order History list now also surfaces the OMS order status (the ECOM status is preferred, with the OMS status as a fallback).

- #2532 `113b4b4` Thanks @vmarta_sfemu! - Rename the engagement adapter from Data Cloud to Data 360, including the config key `engagement.adapters.dataCloud` → `engagement.adapters.data360` (breaking, but pre-GA — no released consumer depends on the old key)

- #2366 `6ea4b59` Thanks @deepali-bharmal_sfemu! - Extend the Page Designer resolution middleware to intercept `getComponent` (`/components/{componentId}`) requests in addition to `getPage` / `getPages`. When `mrtBasedPageDesignerResolution` is enabled and a matching component manifest is in the MRT Data Store, the response is synthesized from the manifest and stamped with `x-component-manifest-hit: 1`. Manifest miss, unpack error, or the feature flag being off falls through to SCAPI unchanged; design/preview mode (`mode` / `pdToken`) is always routed to SCAPI for live content. This brings embedded content block (ECB) caching parity with the previous RSC template.

- #2421 `c1cab51` Thanks @a-mcguire_sfemu! - Bring cartridge generation into schema parity with the Page Designer metadefinition schemas for component/page-type attributes:
  - **`default_component_constructors`**: fixed generation so it conforms to the `componentconstructor` schema. The `@RegionDefinition` decorator authors default constructors as `{ id, typeId, data }`, but the generator previously passed that shape straight through, producing cartridge JSON that fails validation (the schema only permits `type_id`, `name`, and nested `region_component_constructors`, with `additionalProperties: false`). The generator now normalizes `typeId` to a fully-qualified `type_id`, preserves `name`, and drops the schema-invalid `id`/`data` fields.
  - **`searching`**: developers can now declare an attribute's search-index configuration (`searchable`, `refinable`, `boostFactor`, `sortable`) on `@AttributeDefinition`, and the cartridge generator emits it as the schema's `searching` object (with `boostFactor` mapped to `boost_factor`). The schema gates `searching` by attribute type, so generation fails with a clear error when the combination is invalid: `searching` is not allowed on `integer`/`boolean`/`file`/`page`/`image`/`url`/`enum`; `markup` may not set `sortable: true`; and `custom`/`cms_record` may not set `refinable: true`, `boostFactor`, or `sortable: true`.
  - **`dynamicLookup`**: developers can now declare that an attribute sources its value from an aspect attribute by setting `dynamicLookup: { aspectAttributeAlias }` on `@AttributeDefinition`, and the cartridge generator emits it as the schema's `dynamic_lookup` object (mapping `aspectAttributeAlias` to `aspect_attribute_alias`). `dynamic_lookup` is allowed on all attribute types; generation fails with a clear error when `aspectAttributeAlias` is missing.

- #2415 `c173ad5` Thanks @vmarta_sfemu! - Add an out-of-the-box Data Cloud engagement adapter (PWA Kit parity). It builds standard identity + partyIdentification events plus per-event catalog/userEngagement domain events and delivers them to `https://{tenantId}.c360a.salesforce.com/web/events/{appSourceId}/` via `navigator.sendBeacon` (base64 `event=` form body, non-blocking, zero CWV impact). Events are tagged with the shopper's current site (`siteInfo.siteId`, falling back to the configured `siteId`) so multi-site storefronts attribute correctly, and `searchResultTitle` carries the search query (PWA Kit parity) rather than the per-hit product name. Ships with a matching CSP contributor that opens `connect-src` to the exact `https://{tenantId}.c360a.salesforce.com` origin. Registered shoppers now carry `customerId` in the analytics payload for `CC_REGISTERED_CUSTOMER_ID` identity. `sessionId` prefers the `sid` cookie (PWA Kit parity, read fresh per beacon) and falls back to `usid` when `sid` is absent. `view_recommender` events are mapped but dormant until recommender instrumentation exists.

  All three engagement adapters (einstein, activeData, dataCloud) now default to `consentCategory: 'analytics'`, so they fire only when the shopper has granted the `analytics` consent category. With the default binary consent banner this is behavior-preserving; if you clear `consentCategories` to `[]`, the consent layer falls back to `['necessary']`, adapters requiring `'analytics'` will send nothing, and a startup warning is logged (see `README-CONFIG-OPTIONS.md#engagementadaptersadapterconsentcategory`).

- #2458 `a5ed773` Thanks @jangho-jung_sfemu! - Add passkey registration upsell flow. After a shopper registers or logs in, an 8-second toast prompts them to create a passkey if their browser supports WebAuthn and they don't have one yet. Clicking the toast action opens a modal that walks them through passkey creation via the SCAPI WebAuthn registration flow.

  Adds the `clients.auth.passkey` namespace (`authorizeRegistration`, `startRegistration`, `finishRegistration`) to `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime` to back this flow.

- #2458 `7419e3e` Thanks @jangho-jung_sfemu! - Let shoppers name a passkey during creation, and show richer passkey metadata (created date, last-used date, use count, "New" badge) on the account passkeys page.

  Corrects the vendored `PasskeyCredential` schema in `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime` — SCAPI's `getPasskeyUserByLoginId` already returns `aaguid`, `createdTime`, `lastUsed`, and `uses` per credential, but the vendored OpenAPI spec was missing these fields.

  Also hardens the passkey management flow: the account passkeys page 404s when the passkey feature is disabled, the add-passkey entry point surfaces an error on browsers that can't complete WebAuthn registration instead of opening a modal that can only fail, passkey nicknames are validated against SCAPI's 128-character limit on both the client and the start-registration action, deleting an already-absent credential is treated as success, and the delete action no longer triggers a redundant account-loader revalidation.

  Improves passkey UI reliability under slow or failing passkey-status conditions: the "set up a passkey" upsell toast now reads passkey status with a direct fetch and fires from that response, so it no longer gets stuck behind an in-flight page transition; and the account passkeys page renders its heading and "Add Passkey" button immediately, deferring only the credential list — if that list fails to load, an inline message appears in its place rather than blanking the whole page.

- #2032 `25272e5` Thanks @vcua_sfemu! - Add a single `app.cookies.domain` knob for the storefront cookie domain

  A new global config field, `app.cookies.domain`, sets the default `Domain` on **every** cookie the storefront writes — the auth/session cookies and the site-context cookies (`site_id`, locale, currency). Set it once via `PUBLIC__app__cookies__domain=.example.com` instead of redeclaring the entire `commerce.sites` array just to share cookies across subdomains.

  Precedence (applies to all storefront cookies): per-site `commerce.sites[].cookies.domain` → global `app.cookies.domain` → host-only scoping (the default; setting a domain is opt-in). The SDK site-context middleware now applies the resolved per-site domain when serializing the site-context cookies, so the per-site override reaches them too.

  Also fixes the stale `PUBLIC__app__site__cookies__domain` references in the docs (the path never existed).

- #1932 `35d961b` Thanks @mjuraschik_sfemu! - w:

  Embedded Content Blocks (ECB)

  Adds support for fetching and rendering Page Designer components outside
  of a page context. The header is wired up as the first embedded component,
  hosting an `announcement` region for the new announcement banner. Data
  collection for embedded components reuses the same `componentData` promise
  map that pages use, so streaming and per-component Suspense boundaries
  work the same way for both.

- #2051 `606762a` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Add context-aware revalidation for localized SCAPI resource-route fetchers.

  React Router does not surface the evaluated fetcher's identity to a generic resource route's `shouldRevalidate`, so it cannot scope revalidation per-fetcher. `useScapiFetcher` now registers each mounted fetcher's `load` under its encoded `[client, method, options]` key via `createFetcherRegistration(key)` — whose handle exposes `register(…)` and `unregister()` — and the route's `shouldRevalidate` drives reloads from there: on the first call of a mutation-triggered pass it walks the registry, reloads exactly the fetchers a declarative policy (`src/lib/routes/revalidation/api-client.ts`) says the mutation invalidates, and returns `false` to opt out of React Router's blanket auto-revalidation.

  Only `load` is tracked: the registry reloads fetchers, and replaying a `submit` would re-issue a write, so a fetcher's `submit` is never recorded. The shipped policy reloads every fetcher after a global mutation (`setSiteContext`, `updateShopperContext`), and — with the BOPIS extension — reloads store-scoped product fetchers (those reading `query.inventoryIds`) after a store-selection mutation (`setSelectedStore`, `cartPickupStoreUpdate`), since switching the store changes which inventory record a product call reads. Cart mutations do not reload product fetchers: SCAPI reserves inventory at order creation, not on basket changes, so adding to cart never moves a product's availability. Anything else does not reload; a new mutation→fetcher relationship is a single policy entry.

- #2495 `463b2d1` Thanks @vmarta_sfemu! - Track recommendation-carousel impressions and clicks, and report accurate search-result positions across pages.

  **Recommendation analytics now fire.** Impressions and clicks on the "You may also like" recommendation carousels were never being sent to your analytics backends (Data Cloud and Einstein). They now do: an impression is reported once the carousel scrolls into view, and a click is reported when a shopper selects a recommended product. This restores parity with PWA Kit and gives Einstein the engagement signal it needs to improve recommendations.

  **Search and category positions are now global, not per-page.** Previously a product's reported position restarted at the top of every page (the first result on page 3 looked identical to the first result on page 1, always "page 1"). Positions and page numbers are now reported across the full result set, so analytics can distinguish results seen deeper in a listing.

  **Einstein recommendation events are no longer rejected.** The recommendation activity payloads sent to Einstein used the wrong field name and product format, so the endpoints returned errors. Corrected — `viewReco`/`clickReco` now succeed.

- #2451 `373006d` Thanks @harshini-magesh_sfemu! - Add two surface-specific `<UITarget>` slots inside the shared `OrderSummary` component, rendered below the "Order Summary" heading and above the Subtotal/Shipping/Total lines: `sfcc.cart.orderSummary.body.before` (cart) and `sfcc.checkout.orderSummary.body.before` (checkout).

  `OrderSummary` gains an optional `surface?: 'cart' | 'checkout'` prop that selects which slot renders; the cart page passes `surface="cart"` and checkout passes `surface="checkout"`. Surfaces that pass no `surface` (the mobile order-summary accordion and account order details) expose neither slot. The slots render nothing until an extension targets them — no DOM and no runtime cost when unconsumed. The pre-existing generic `sfcc.{cart,checkout}.orderSummary.before` slots (which render above the whole card) are unchanged and remain available to other extensions.

- #2454 `959a001` Thanks @harshini-magesh_sfemu! - Fetch approaching-discount data on the single shared basket fetch by opting into `expand=approaching_discounts` in the basket middleware. The expand rides on the existing `getBasket` fetch every surface (mini-cart, cart, checkout) already makes, so `basket.approachingDiscounts` is populated with no extra SCAPI round-trip. The template decides which expansions to request; the SDK basket helper only threads the query through.

- #2458 `b0fb707` Thanks @jangho-jung_sfemu! - Add passkey login via WebAuthn conditional mediation on `/login` and the checkout contact-info step. Shoppers with a saved passkey for the origin see it as an autofill suggestion on the email field instead of needing to enter a password. The successful standard-password-login redirect now uses `redirectDocument` instead of `redirect` — a client-side transition never unloads the document, so a native passkey picker left open by conditional mediation would otherwise stay visible on the next page after login.

- #2140 `6b1a548` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Switch checkout revalidation from a boolean opt-out to tag-based opt-in; remove `FRAMEWORK_SKIP_REVALIDATION` export.

  The checkout route now declares `CHECKOUT_REVALIDATE_TAGS = ['checkout.update']` as its data-dependency vocabulary. Extension actions opt in to triggering a checkout-loader reload by returning `revalidateTags: ['checkout.update']` on their action result (or using the `withRevalidateTags` helper). An action that returns no matching tags skips the loader reload, so adoption is incremental - actions that previously used `framework_skipRevalidation: true` get the same "do not reload" behaviour automatically until they are updated.

  **Migration**: the `FRAMEWORK_SKIP_REVALIDATION` constant is no longer exported from `@/lib/revalidation/routes/checkout`. Remove any import of it and remove `framework_skipRevalidation: true` from action results. To suppress the checkout-loader reload, return a `revalidateTags` value that does not intersect with `CHECKOUT_REVALIDATE_TAGS` - for example `revalidateTags: ['checkout.payment.complete']`. To trigger a reload, include `'checkout.update'` in `revalidateTags`.

- #2255 `3b2806c` Thanks @madhuri-uppu_sfemu! - Replace the legacy ECV1/MIAW Embedded Messaging (shopper-agent) with the Cimulate Commerce Client messaging widget. The new integration uses requestIdleCallback-deferred loading to avoid blocking hydration, derives CSP origins from config, and validates script URLs against trusted Cimulate domains.

- #2366 `6ea4b59` Thanks @deepali-bharmal_sfemu! - Add `ComponentManifest` type and `ManifestStorage.getComponentManifest` for the embedded-component (ECB) read path. Introduces a base `Manifest` interface (with `manifestType`, `context`, `componentInfo`) extended by both `PageManifest` and the new `ComponentManifest`, mirroring the backend hierarchy in `commerce/digital`. - #2042 `c0b87fb` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Shopper agent (Embedded Messaging) now contributes its exact configured origins to the CSP instead of relying on broad wildcards. The security middleware accepts boot-static CSP contributors; the template ships a shopper-agent contributor that derives script/frame/connect origins from `commerceAgent` config. - #2471 `c1ed55f` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Add a `commerce.sitesFromDal` flag (default on) that sources `commerce.sites` from the unified DAL sites entry. When on and the DAL entry is present, a new request middleware rewrites the site config for site/locale/currency resolution; otherwise the static config stands.

  Because the flag ships enabled, site/locale/currency resolution reads from the DAL sites entry once the matching Business Manager sync is enabled — making the DAL the source of truth for site configuration in that setup. If the DAL entry is missing, unavailable, or yields no usable sites, resolution falls back to the static `commerce.sites` in `config.server.ts`. To keep the static config authoritative regardless of the DAL, set `commerce.sitesFromDal` to `false` (or `PUBLIC__app__commerce__sitesFromDal=false`).

  `readLazyDataStoreEntry` now logs a warning when it finds no registered loader in context, so a lazy data-store middleware that is missing from (or misordered in) the request chain surfaces as a debuggable misconfiguration instead of a silent no-op.

- #1937 `6c57057` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Auto-discover extension config files. An extension can now ship a `src/extensions/<name>/config.ts` that default-exports its client-side config defaults, and the framework discovers it at build time, merges it into `config.app.extension.<camelCaseFolder>`, and derives the TypeScript type automatically — no edits to `config.server.ts` or `src/types/config.ts`. Merchants override per environment with `PUBLIC__app__extension__<key>__<setting>`. Adds the `sfnext config aggregate-extensions` CLI prestep (run by `pnpm dev`, `pnpm build`, and `pnpm typecheck`), mirroring the existing extension locale aggregation.

- #2033 `2d8baef` Thanks @daniel-diaz_sfemu! - Neutralize shadcn shape tokens via --ui-radius, --ui-shadow, --ui-border-width overrides, enabling per-vertical theming of Card corners, elevation, and border widths without editing component source

- #2401 `5aba6f4` Thanks @jie-dai_sfemu! - Add shopper-facing item-level order return and full-order cancellation on the Order Details page, backed by SCAPI's OMS surface. Eligible orders surface **Return Items** and **Cancel Order** actions in the top action bar; both open dialogs that read live OMS metadata (`getOmsMetaData`) for per-item eligibility, remaining returnable/cancelable quantity, and reason codes, then submit through `returnOmsOrder` / `cancelOmsOrder` with per-item quantities and optional reasons. The return dialog supports partial returns, per-item reason selection, mobile drawer layout, feedback/error recovery states, and a reasons-unavailable path that keeps the Review button enabled and omits `reason` so the server applies its default.

  Order badge colors follow UX guidance — green for created/new/completed/replaced, red for cancelled and failed, blue/info for the two in-progress return states (`RETURN_INITIATED`, `PARTIAL_RETURN_INITIATED`) so shoppers can distinguish an in-flight return from a settled one, and neutral gray for the two complete return states (`RETURN_COMPLETE`, `PARTIAL_RETURN_COMPLETE`), derived per-unit from `quantityOrdered`, `quantityCanceled`, `quantityReturned`, and `quantityReturnInitiated`.

  Unavailable Return Items / Cancel Order actions now render as disabled buttons (matching PWA Kit) rather than being hidden — the button stays visible but carries `aria-disabled`, a click guard, and an sr-only reason (`orders.returnUnavailable` / `orders.cancelUnavailable`) linked via `aria-describedby` so assistive tech can still discover it (Sharks review,). Track Shipment is unchanged — it still renders only when a real tracking target exists. The regenerated Shopper Orders types (OAS v1.17.1) renamed the OMS shipment schema `schemas-Shipment` → `OmsShipment` and widened `Order.channelType` with a `"chatgpt"` value past `Basket.channelType`; the order-summary promo-code form renders for baskets only, so the basket cast is narrowed accordingly.

  Ships a customer-facing `docs/README-ORDER-MANAGEMENT.md` covering the return, cancel, and tracking flows, status-badge derivation, and where refunds happen (SOM-owned, out of storefront scope). `parseTrackingDate` gains a third guard rejecting truthy epoch-era date strings (`getUTCFullYear() <= 1970`) so a `1970-01-01`-style sentinel never renders as "Jan 1, 1970".

- #2196 `1503ac0` Thanks @sprasoon_sfemu! - Add OMS shipment tracking to the Order Details page. When an order has Salesforce Order Management tracking data, each shipment shows the tracking number as a link to the carrier's tracking page, the carrier name, and the expected and actual delivery dates; a "Track shipment" action links straight to the carrier (or to the tracking section when no carrier link is available). Orders without OMS data continue to show the existing tracking number and status. The Order History list now also surfaces the OMS order status (the ECOM status is preferred, with the OMS status as a fallback).

  Carrier tracking-link normalization is hardened against host-confusion: a tracking URL shaped `label.tld://host/path` is rejected instead of being rewritten into a link that reads like one host but navigates to another; genuine scheme-less `host:port` values continue to resolve normally. When the only tracking entry has a carrier URL that cannot be turned into a safe external link (and no tracking number, provider, or delivery date), the "Track shipment" action is hidden rather than linking to a tracking section that will not render.

- #2283 `1440c19` Thanks @sprasoon_sfemu! - Add a **Track Shipment** action to the top order-actions row on the Order Details page. The affordance adapts to the order's tracking data: a single carrier link deep-links to the carrier in a new tab; a tracking-number-only shipment links to the in-page tracking section; and multiple carrier links become a dropdown so the shopper picks which to open. When an order has no usable tracking target, the action renders nothing and the order-actions row collapses (`empty:hidden`) rather than showing a disabled control. Carrier links reuse the same `ensureExternalUrl` hardening as the in-section tracking links.

  Also corrects the `OrderTracking` doc comment that listed shipment status among the card's rendered fields (status is shown by a separate badge). The dropdown option labels use distinct interpolation variables per branch: `{{trackingNumber}}` for a real tracking string and `{{number}}` for the 1-based positional fallback, so a translator styling a tracking string cannot corrupt the positional-integer copy.

  The new `account.orders.actions.*` strings ship as English placeholders in the non-English locale files; real translations follow from localization.

- #2262 `d559c98` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Add a `billingAddressGetter` field to `PaymentSubmissionRef`. Payment extensions that replace the `sfcc.checkout.payment` UI target and register `onPlaceOrder` can register this getter to hand the shopper's current billing address back to the checkout page; the checkout persists it to `basket.billingAddress` via a new `/resource/update-basket-billing-address` route before delegating to `onPlaceOrder`. The default form-based Payment component registers a getter that returns the currently-typed billing address when "billing differs" is checked and `null` otherwise, so existing storefronts see no behavior change.

- #2419 `16903fb` Thanks @madhuri-uppu_sfemu! - Add a "Load more" pagination mode to the product listing page as a merchant-configurable alternative to numbered pagination.
  - **Mode toggle** (`uiConfig.pages.category.pagination.mode`): `load-more` (default) or `traditional`.
  - **Load more + infinite scroll**: appends the next batch in place via a non-navigating fetch to a new `/resource/category-products` endpoint, keeping the initial page's critical/non-critical streaming intact; auto-loads as the shopper scrolls near the end, with the button as an accessible manual trigger and fallback.
  - **Responsive batch size**: smaller batch on mobile (12) than desktop (24); full-width, large-tap-target button on mobile.
  - **Performance cap**: stops at a configurable DOM cap (default 200 products) and prompts the shopper to refine filters.
  - **End-of-catalog** message when all products are loaded.
  - **Scroll restoration**: persists loaded count to `sessionStorage` (keyed by React Router's `history.state.key`) so back-navigation renders a skeleton grid at the correct height, lets `ScrollRestoration` restore the scroll position, then catch-up fetches fill in the real tiles; resets and scrolls to top on filter/sort change.
  - **SEO**: server-rendered `rel="next"`/`rel="prev"` link tags and a `?page=N` crawler fallback so bots can discover the whole result set.
  - **Accessibility**: `aria-busy` on the grid during fetch, `aria-live` progress announcements, and focus moved to the first newly appended tile after each load.

  Built with the design-system `Button` and `Spinner`; new products fade in (200ms, motion-safe).

- #2096 `89c07df` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Upgrade react-router and @react-router/\* to 7.18.0. Patches an unauthenticated RCE plus four other advisories in the vendored turbo-stream dependency.

  **ACTION REQUIRED (security):** This advisory is only patched once your project resolves `react-router` / `@react-router/*` at `>= 7.18.0`. The SDK declares react-router as a peer dependency, so the version is pinned by your own `package.json`, not by the SDK — bumping `@salesforce/storefront-next-*` alone does not pull the fix. Bump react-router and `@react-router/*` to `7.18.0` in your project's `package.json`. Projects generated fresh from the template already get `7.18.0`.

  This release also renames React Router APIs that stabilized in 7.15 (dropping their `unstable_` prefix). `unstable_optimizeDeps` stays unstable and is unchanged.

  **ACTION REQUIRED — if you ejected `entry.server.tsx` and export your own instrumentations:** React Router 7.18 reads the server-entry export named `instrumentations`, not `unstable_instrumentations`. The framework matches this export by name, so the old name still compiles — it just silently stops registering your instrumentation. Rename `export const unstable_instrumentations` to `export const instrumentations`.

  The remaining renames surface as `pnpm typecheck` errors, so they're caught at build time: `unstable_ServerInstrumentation` → `ServerInstrumentation` (type), route arg `unstable_pattern` → `pattern`, `future.unstable_subResourceIntegrity` → top-level `subResourceIntegrity`, `future.unstable_trailingSlashAwareDataRequests` → `future.v8_trailingSlashAwareDataRequests`, `future.unstable_passThroughRequests` → `future.v8_passThroughRequests`.

  Loader/action/middleware arg _types_ now include a `url: URL` field (RR 7.18 type change). Runtime behavior is unchanged — the framework still provides URLs via `request.url`; only types and test fixtures needed updating. No production loader/action change is required.

- #1900 `39b9c15` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Wire SDK security-headers middleware into the React Router middleware chain. Apply per-request CSP nonce to the inline `__APP_CONFIG__` script. New customer-facing doc: `docs/README-SECURITY-HEADERS.md`.

- #1964 `4fe15ff` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Auto-discover server-only extension config. Parallel to the existing `config.ts` aggregator, an extension can now ship a `src/extensions/<name>/server-config.ts` that default-exports its server-only defaults — vendor SCAPI overrides, retry budgets, internal endpoints — and the framework merges them into `config.app.serverExtension.<camelCaseFolder>`, reachable via `getConfig(context).serverExtension.<key>` from server loaders, actions, and middleware. Values never reach the browser: the root loader strips `app.serverExtension` before React Router serializes the SSR hydration payload, and a Vite plugin fails the build if any client chunk imports the generated barrel. The existing `sfnext config aggregate-extensions` CLI now writes both barrels (`index.ts` and `server.ts`) in one run via `Promise.all` — no second command, no second prestep. There is intentionally no `PUBLIC__` override path — the same AST validator forbids `process.env`, so true secrets must continue to be read from `process.env` in a server route.

- #1866 `4238f07` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Add `action.place-order-prepare` and `action.place-order-finalize` so payment extensions plug in via the `onPlaceOrder` ref without owning non-payment checkout work. The storefront's Place Order click handler now POSTs to `prepare` (basket validation, multiship resolution, totals refresh), awaits the extension's callback for createOrder + PSP confirmation, then POSTs to `finalize` (shopper-scope check, profile saves, basket teardown, navigation).

- #2252 `2a02f00` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Fix DIS-eligibility check to anchor the `/dw/image/v2/` path match to `url.pathname` and gate it on a host-capability check.

  Previously the predicate tested the full URL string with an unanchored regex and never verified the host, so query strings, fragments, or third-party hosts carrying `/dw/image/v2/` in the path (e.g. `?ref=/dw/image/v2/foo`, `#/dw/image/v2/section`, `https://thirdparty.com/dw/image/v2/x.jpg`) were misclassified as DIS-eligible, received `sfrm`/`q`/`sw` parameters, and 404'd.

  Now a URL is DIS-eligible only when the `/dw/image/v2/` prefix appears at the start of the pathname **and** the host is DIS-capable — it matches `config.images.host`, a `config.images.realmHostMappings` entry, or a built-in SFCC domain (`.commercecloud.salesforce.com`, `.demandware.net`, `.my.cc.salesforce.com`). The `?sfrm=` branch is gated on the same host-check, so a spoofed `sfrm` parameter on a third-party host no longer forces eligibility. Vanity domains without a `realmHostMappings` entry now fail closed.

- #1867 `e751c22` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - **Prevent CloudFront from caching server errors on data requests.** A new middleware sets a caching header on server-error responses (status 500–504) so CloudFront doesn't keep serving a stale error after the underlying problem is fixed. Most of these errors are marked "do not store" — except 503, which is allowed to cache for just two seconds. A 503 signals that the backend is temporarily overloaded (SCAPI load shedding), so a very short shared cache acts as a system-wide cool-down that shields the origin from a retry stampede while still clearing within seconds. The behavior is scoped to React Router single-fetch data interactions (the client-side navigations and fetcher calls that hit `.data` URLs and return a turbo-stream payload); full-page document responses are left untouched, so CloudFront's default error caching still acts as a backoff that shields the origin during traffic spikes. A data interaction is detected from either the `.data` request URL suffix or React Router's single-fetch response marker, so detection keeps working both today and after a future React Router upgrade preserves the suffix on the request. Note: this also requires a configuration change on the CDN side (setting the error caching TTL to zero for those status codes), because the CDN won't fully respect the origin's caching headers on its own.

The `resolvedContext` entry now preserves each resolved data binding's `type → id → field → value` structure instead of collapsing bindings to a list of field names, truncating long string values to a reasonable length so the log conveys the content without emitting large payloads. Tracked under.

- #1886 `953164d` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Add observability log lines for two otherwise-hard-to-track SCAPI failure categories. This is detection and logging only — no automatic retries.
  - **SCAPI under heavy load (load shedding).** A new wrapper inspects a special header that SCAPI includes in its responses to indicate how busy it is. When the server advertises pressure on a request it still serves, a warning is logged; when the server actually rejects the request with a 503, an error is logged. Both include the request URL (with sensitive parts masked) and the load percentage when available.
  - **Rate limiting (HTTP 429).** When SCAPI responds with a 429 ("too many requests"), an error is logged including the request URL and the raw `Retry-After` value the server sent (if any).

  Both share a common `SCAPI health` marker in the log message so they can be pulled from logs with a single search. The logs only fire for actual network responses — not for results served from a local cache.

(2) The button no longer gates on `!form.formState.isValid` either; React Hook Form's `handleSubmit` already short-circuits on invalid forms and the inline field errors give the shopper feedback. Removing this gate also unblocks validation E2E scenarios that intentionally submit invalid input to assert error rendering. Re-enables 34 E2E checkout scenarios across 10 spec files that were skipped under.

The denylist is conservative: mutations that DO feed the loader — `addReview`, store/pickup changes (availability), the currency switch, and shopper-context updates (pricing/promotions) — stay off the list and still revalidate, and any unlisted mutation revalidates by default.

Cart, promo, bonus, and pickup mutations still revalidate.

- #2015 `f79538c` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Add a `shouldRevalidate` gate to the `resource.reviews-summary` route so the rating-summary fetcher no longer re-runs on unrelated action submissions. - #2102 `34a3d4e` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Bump runtime dependencies for security remediation.
  - `js-cookie` `3.0.5` → `3.0.8` (direct dependency)

The dev-only `@lhci/cli` brings `express@4`, whose `Layer` constructor calls `path-to-regexp` as a function and breaks against the v8 object-shape export; that one chain carries a scope-narrowed `express@4>path-to-regexp` exception back to `0.1.13` (the function-shape patch that also fixes GHSA-37ch-88jc-xwx2) so `pnpm lighthouse:ci` still boots.

- #2095 `9438b9d` Thanks @jie-dai_sfemu! - Fix promo codes showing a false "applied" state when valid but ineligible for the cart. Ineligible/rejected codes now surface a status-specific error with the correct 4xx status instead of a phantom discount or a misreported 500.

- #2101 `9cb7384` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - perf(revalidation): scope cart revalidation across the basket-products resource

  The always-mounted cart badge kept the `/resource/basket-products` fetcher registered, so React Router revalidated it — a SCAPI round-trip — after every basket mutation, even with the panel closed and nothing rendering its products. Its `shouldRevalidate` now gates the post-action reload on the panel being mounted, and otherwise catches up on the next panel-open or hover/focus prefetch via a staleness check. When a full basket has been loaded into `BasketProvider` (the add/edit/remove handlers and the mini-cart's own publish-back effect write the action-response basket, which carries the SCAPI `lastModified`), the check compares `lastModified` — so a count-neutral change such as a variant swap is detected on reopen. When only the cookie snapshot is available (returning visitor, nothing mutated this session, panel never opened), it falls back to a count-identity diff (`basketId` + total quantity + unique line count), reusing the warm cache when the counts match and reloading when they diverge; a count-neutral cross-tab change is the one narrow gap, and the next route loader reconciles it via the basket middleware.

  The open-panel staleness check is now directional. When the panel is open, `resource.basket-products`' `shouldRevalidate` already revalidates the fetcher after a basket mutation; the `BasketProvider` freshness reference (`useBasket`) trails that fetcher by one render, because the publish-back is a parent `setState` that cannot converge within the same commit. The check compared `lastModified` with a symmetric `!==`, so it read that benign render-lag (fetcher newer than reference) as staleness and fired a redundant second `/resource/basket-products` request. It now reloads only when the reference is strictly newer than the cached data — a revision the cache hasn't pulled yet — and treats an older reference as render-lag, not staleness. `lastModified` is SCAPI's ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, so the lexicographic comparison is chronological.

  The mini-cart's UI state (`open` plus `panelMounted`) moves into one external store (`src/hooks/mini-cart-store.ts`, `useSyncExternalStore` with slice selectors), replacing the former `MiniCartContext` and the standalone visibility flag. It serves both a reactive in-React read and the synchronous read `shouldRevalidate` needs from outside the React tree, and imports only `react` so the route module stays free of client-only dependencies and import cycles.

- #2132 `7af1edb` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Fix the dev hybrid proxy to handle every `url.prefix` shape out of the box, so a locale-prefixed legacy path (e.g. `/uk/cart`) is no longer double-stacked into `/s/{siteId}/{locale}/uk/cart`.

  The dev proxy unconditionally prepended `/s/{defaultSiteId}/{locale}` to every non-SFRA path. Now that the template emits prefixed paths (`/uk/cart`, `/global/en-GB/cart`), that stacked the locale a second time and SFRA 404'd. The proxy now reads `app.url.prefix` and the site/locale alias catalog from `config.server.ts`, strips the prefix the URL already carries, and reuses that site/locale when decorating to SFRA's `/s/{siteId}/{locale}/…` shape — for no prefix, `/:localeId`, and `/:siteId/:localeId` alike. A captured segment is only treated as a site/locale when it is a known identifier, so a bare legacy path (`/cart` under `/:localeId`) isn't mistaken for a locale home. The root `/` maps to the locale-less SFRA site root and the query string is preserved across the rewrite.

  `hybridProxyPlugin` gains optional `urlPrefix`, `siteAliases`, `localeAliases`, and a last-resort `rewritePath` escape hatch for non-standard URL models. `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime` exports a new `extractPrefixParamValues` site-context helper (mirrors `stripPathPrefix`'s matching rules) that powers the prefix-aware rewrite.

- #2115 `eab5649` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Publish the updated basket revision from the bonus-product modal, bonus-product carousel direct-add, promo-code apply/remove, cart quantity-update, and cart-line remove handlers so `useBasket()` consumers (badge, mini-cart freshness reference) stay in sync after these mutations, matching the add/edit/remove handlers.

- #2210 `8e720bf` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Add lazy data-store preference middleware and an opt-in cross-request L1 cache to cut DynamoDB reads on the single shared data-store partition

  The eager `dataStoreMiddleware` reads all four preference entries on every request that reaches root, even routes that never use them. All entries share one partition key (`"${MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID} ${DEPLOY_TARGET}"`), so that volume can throttle one physical partition under load.

  The new lazy variants (`customSitePreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, `customGlobalPreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, `gcpPreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, `loginPreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, their `get*Lazy` accessors, and the `dataStoreMiddlewareLazy` bundle) register a memoized loader instead of fetching up front, so the read fires only when a loader reads the value and repeat reads within a request share the promise. The eager exports are deprecated but unchanged. The template wires `dataStoreMiddlewareLazy`, reads login preferences via the async `getLoginPreferences` wrapper, and moves the GCP Address Autocomplete API key onto the checkout loader (the only route mounting `GoogleCloudApiProvider`).

  The L1 cache serves repeat reads of the same entry from memory. It lives on `globalThis` (via a `Symbol.for` key) to survive SSR module re-evaluation and persist across a warm Lambda's sequential requests. Only successful reads of deployment-/site-scoped preference entries are cached — never shopper data, fallbacks, missing entries, or errors; `getDataStoreEntry` stays a thin, cache-free read. It is off by default; set `MRT_DATA_STORE_CACHE_ENABLED=true` to opt in per environment (e.g. deployed MRT). `MRT_DATA_STORE_CACHE_TTL` sets the TTL in ms (default 300000) and `MRT_DATA_STORE_CACHE_MAXBYTES` the total-value byte budget (default 131072); zero/negative/non-numeric falls back to the default. The cache is bounded by byte size, not entry count, evicting least-recently-used keys. `clearDataStoreCache()` drops the instance for test isolation or to force-bust a warm container after a preference publish.

- #2144 `19beba8` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - perf(nav): fix whole-page hydration flicker caused by the mobile navigation drawer

  `MobileMenuDropdown` rendered its category list unconditionally and only hid it with CSS while the menu was closed. Each `MobileMenuCategory` subscribes to the sub-category store via `useSubCategory` (a `useSyncExternalStore` consumer), so those subscribers were present in the SSR/hydration tree even though the drawer was invisible. When the deferred sub-category promise resolved post-hydration and filled the store, the subscribers re-rendered, and because the header sits above `<Outlet/>` the re-render cascaded into a visible full-page flicker on every page.

  The drawer now mounts its subtree only while the menu is open, keeping the store subscribers out of the initial render. This matches the desktop mega panel, whose subscribers already live inside the lazily-mounted Radix content. No behavior change when the menu is open.

- #2145 `eadc14f` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - perf(wishlist): fix whole-page hydration flicker caused by WishlistProvider

  `WishlistProvider` deferred its SCAPI hydration to a post-mount `useEffect`, then wrote the resolved customer/list IDs into `useState` via `setHydrated`. That state update re-rendered the provider, which rebuilt the `useScapiFetchClient` add/remove hooks (the customer/list IDs were baked into their URLs at construction), changed the identities of the `add`/`remove`/`toggle` callbacks, produced a new `actions` value, and so changed the `WishlistActionsContext` value. Every `useWishlistActions` consumer in the page subtree re-rendered at once — a visible full-page flicker on every route that mounts a `WishlistProvider`.

  The provider no longer stores the customer/list IDs in React state. They live on a ref that the hydration effect updates without a re-render, and `add` supplies them per call via a `params` override (mirroring how `remove` already passed the item-keyed path). The `add`/`remove` dependency arrays shrink to `[store]`, so the `add`/`remove`/`toggle` callbacks stay referentially stable for the provider's lifetime and hydration no longer rebuilds them. Hydration still fills the store via `replaceAll`, which only re-renders the topic subscribers (heart icons) whose entries actually changed. No behavior change for guests or for the add/remove/toggle flows.

- #2181 `ea71ca0` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Build the navigation mega menu's sub category structure with a single `getCategories` request instead of one `getCategory` request per root category. This reduces the number of SCAPI calls per initial page load from N+1 to 1+ceil(N/50) and positions the menu to benefit from SCAPI response caching. Category IDs are chunked into groups of 50 (the endpoint limit).

- #2194 `c1b3737` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Stabilize product tile rendering during hydration.

  The featured products carousel on the home page visually re-render on hydration, causing a visible flicker. `ProductTileProvider` derived a `swatchMode` (`'click'` / `'hover'`) from a `useSyncExternalStore` whose server snapshot was always `'click'` while the client snapshot was `'hover'` on desktop viewports — so hydration always produced a reconciliation re-render, and because `swatchMode` was a field of the context value, that flip re-rendered every tile in the grid. The value was only ever read inside the swatch-hover handler, never during render, so the entire subscription was render churn for a value that could be read on demand.

  Replace the `swatchMode` context field and its `useSyncExternalStore` subscription with an `isDesktopViewport()` helper read at hover time. The tile's hover handler now queries the viewport synchronously when the user hovers a swatch instead of subscribing to it during render, eliminating the post-hydration flip. The `ProductTileContext` value (both the provider and the `useProductTileContext` fallback path) is memoized so its reference changes only when a field consumers read actually changes, letting memoized consumers bail out.

Overlay text now sits on a darker scrim so it stays legible over any merchant photo; the images themselves are unchanged.

- #2236 `7cc1a33` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Fix `<DynamicImage>` so it only applies DIS transformation to URLs the imaging service can actually serve. With DIS enabled, the shared resolver keyed format conversion, quality, and `sw`/`sh` params off "is this an absolute URL" — but a relative bundled asset (`/images/hero-01.webp`) or a non-SFCC host (`https://via.placeholder.com/300`) has no derivable realm, so `toDisBaseUrl` returns it unchanged and it never becomes a DIS URL. The resolver was still emitting a `<picture>` with dead `?sw=&q=` `<source>` variants and rewriting the `<img>` fallback to a non-existent path (`/images/hero-01.jpg?sfrm=webp` — a 404). It now gates DIS on whether the URL was actually rewritten into `/dw/image/v2/{realm}/`: relative and third-party URLs render verbatim in their own format with no conversion or query params, while a high-priority local image still emits a single `<link rel="preload">` so LCP heroes keep their preload hint. Genuine DIS-hosted SFCC URLs are unaffected.

- #2257 `db6f254` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Render the hero banner image through `<DynamicImage priority="high" loading="eager">` instead of a raw `<img fetchPriority="high">`. The raw `<img>` emitted no preload hint (`fetchPriority` only reprioritizes a fetch after the element is discovered during body parse), so the LCP hero was invisible to the preload scanner during SSR, and it bypassed DIS entirely — downloading the full-size original at every viewport. `<DynamicImage>` triggers React 19's SSR `preload()` to hoist a `<link rel="preload" as="image" fetchpriority="high">` into the streamed `<head>` and serves a responsive, DIS-optimized `<picture>`, aligning the hero with every other image in the storefront. Focal point (`object-position`), `object-cover`, and the full-bleed absolute-fill layout are preserved.

- #2258 `3f6c24f` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Render hero carousel slide images through `<DynamicImage>` instead of raw `<img fetchPriority="high">`. The raw `<img>` emitted no preload hint (`fetchPriority` only reprioritizes a fetch after the element is discovered during body parse), so the first slide — the LCP candidate — was invisible to the preload scanner during SSR, and every slide bypassed DIS entirely, downloading the full-size original at each viewport. Slides now render as responsive, DIS-optimized `<picture>` elements. Only the first slide is preloaded and loaded eagerly (`priority="high"` / `loading="eager"`), so React 19's SSR `preload()` hoists a `<link rel="preload" as="image" fetchpriority="high">` into the streamed `<head>`; the off-screen slides stay lazy so they don't compete with the LCP image for bandwidth. The `object-cover` full-bleed layout is preserved.

- #2357 `fc9ba33` Thanks @s-mahajan_sfemu! - Surface estimated delivery dates on multi-shipment checkout shipping options. When a shipping method returns a `deliveryWindow` (`startAt`/`endAt` RFC 3339 timestamps), the multiship shipping selector and its summary now display the formatted date range, matching single-shipment shipping options. Falls back to `c_estimatedArrivalTime` when `deliveryWindow` is absent.

- #2300 `9fb7230` Thanks @vcua_sfemu! - fix(page-designer): resolve getPages 400 on PLP/PDP without breaking category fallback

  The PDP loader passes a `primaryCategoryId` fallback alongside `productId`. `fetchPage`'s `getPages` branch forwarded both to SCAPI's `/pages` endpoint, which rejects calls carrying multiple business-object IDs with `400 business-object-id-invalid` — ~369K of the 400s seen in load testing.

  `fetchPage` now sends only the most specific business-object ID to `getPages` (`productId` if present, otherwise `categoryId`), while still carrying the full set in the `aspectAttributes` JSON. The MRT page-resolution middleware's `getPages` branch now reads its aspect attributes from that JSON (falling back to the top-level params), so the category-level page fallback — a PDP whose product has no page but whose primary category does — keeps working on the manifest path.

- #2320 `3ec7bf7` Thanks @vmarta_sfemu! - w:

  Ship the React Router 7.18 migration guide in the template docs. The guide lived
  at the monorepo-root `docs/`, which the template mirror never publishes, so it
  never reached customers. Moved it to `packages/template/docs/migrations/react-router-7.18/README.md`
  (a mirrored path) and linked it from the template doc indexes. Also added a
  `docs/README.md` marker documenting that root `docs/` is internal-only.

- #2323 `905cd24` Thanks @cboscenco_sfemu! - Fix an intermittent i18n hydration mismatch by deferring client hydration until the active language's translations have loaded. The server renders translated text, but the client i18next instance loads translations asynchronously; if React hydrated first, the initial client render showed fallback keys and diverged from the SSR HTML. A custom `entry.client.tsx` now awaits `whenI18nReady()` (the same async locale load, capped by a timeout so a slow/failed chunk still hydrates) before calling `hydrateRoot`. This adds no bytes to the document — it only reorders client startup — so it fixes the mismatch without regressing document transfer size.

- #2399 `e4d96a9` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - feat(auth): restore header auth state under a cached app shell via a userType hint cookie

  Under app-shell caching, a shared non-personalized HTML document is served from the eCDN; on a cache HIT the origin does not run, so the loader-baked `userType` freezes for the whole TTL window and every visitor sees whatever auth state was cached (typically the neutral guest value). The header's Sign In vs. My Account link and the wishlist icon's target path would then be wrong for signed-in shoppers.

  This adds the client-hint plumbing that lets those consumers self-correct on the client without any per-consumer edits:
  - **`lib/auth/user-type-hint.ts`** — the `__sfdc_usertype` cookie-name constant plus a shape validator that accepts only `guest`/`registered` (a JS-readable cookie is user-editable, so a tampered value is dropped) and a site-namespaced parser that reads through the shared `parseCookie` helper, mirroring the currency/basket companion cookies' posture.
  - **`middlewares/user-type-hint.server.ts`** — a dedicated response-phase middleware that writes `__sfdc_usertype` (`httpOnly:false`, auto-namespaced `_{siteId}`, base64(JSON) on the wire like the currency/basket cookies) from the final per-request session, so a just-completed login is reflected. It writes the `userType` flag **only** — never the httpOnly token cookies (`cc-at`, `cc-nx`, `cc-nx-g`, `usid`) or `customerId`/`encUserId`. The hint is strictly less than what the SSR hydration payload already exposes. On a logged-out/destroyed session (resolved but with no `userType`) it **expires** any stale hint with `expires: new Date(0)`, mirroring the auth middleware's cookie cleanup — otherwise the year-long `registered` hint would mis-restore a signed-in header for a now-guest shopper on a cached shell. When auth never resolves (early error response) it leaves any existing hint untouched.
  - **`providers/auth.tsx`** — `AuthProvider` gains a client-side fallback that overrides `userType` only, read from the hint cookie via `useSyncExternalStore` with asymmetric snapshots (server/first-hydration return `null`, so no hydration-mismatch warning; the cookie is read post-hydration and wins over the frozen loader value). It takes a new optional `siteId` prop to resolve the namespaced cookie — passed explicitly (rather than read from `SiteProvider`) so the provider stays free of a mount-order coupling; when omitted the fallback is inert.
  - **Consumers** (`header/user-actions`, `header/wishlist-icon`) now gate on `userType === 'registered'` only. The former `&& customerId` check was a defensive no-op (both derive from the same JWT) and would actively break restoration under caching, since the hint never carries `customerId`.

  No behavior change on uncached routes: the hint merely confirms the loader value.

- #2350 `d3d756a` Thanks @jcesarpierre_sfemu! - Serve the `public/` directory in Storybook so stories that reference image assets by URL render correctly

- #2383 `1d2ee5a` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Fix `WishlistListItem` keeping its "Select options" modal mounted forever after the first open. The modal was gated on a sticky `isSelectOptionsModalLoaded` latch that never reset, so the modal's `useScapiFetcher` product/variant fetchers stayed registered in the fetcher registry after close and were re-run on every subsequent context mutation (currency/locale/site switch, store selection) — amplified per wishlist row. The modal now gates on `open` via the `useDeferredUnmount` hook that keeps it mounted briefly after close so the Radix exit animation plays, then unmounts it so the fetchers deregister.

- #2384 `36e077c` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Fix the account-details OTP modal staying mounted for the rest of the session after the first email-edit or verify-email flow. The `OtpModal` was gated on a sticky `otpModalLoaded` latch that flipped true on open and never reset, so once opened its `useFetcher`, resend-countdown timer, OTP-input ref pool, and effects lingered in the React tree indefinitely after the shopper closed or completed the flow. The modal now gates on `isOpen` via the shared `useDeferredUnmount` hook, keeping the subtree mounted briefly after close so the Radix exit animation plays, then unmounting it so its fetcher, timer, and effects tear down.

- #2418 `d11c7f4` Thanks @michael-mcmahon_sfemu! - Migrate linting and formatting from ESLint + Prettier to OxLint + Biome . `pnpm lint` remains the single entry point CI calls — it now runs OxLint (`--type-aware --max-warnings 0`, plus the custom `custom/*` rules) followed by a Biome format check. The migration introduces no functional lint or formatting gaps: the ESLint rule surface (including the verticals boundary rule, the browser-only `i18n/client` import restriction, and the copyright-header and color-token rules, now `custom/header-format` and `custom/color-linter`) is reproduced in `.oxlintrc.json`, and formatting moves wholesale to Biome. `.eslintrc`/`eslint.config.js`/`.prettierrc` and their per-package variants are removed; `.oxlintrc.json` + `biome.json` are added at the root and per package. The template's lint/format doc is renamed `README-ESLINT.md` → `README-LINTING.md` to match the new toolchain.

  SDK-side, generated customer-project files are now emitted in Biome's byte shape (new `formatWithProjectBiome`/`formatDirectoryWithProjectBiome` helpers, resolving the consuming project's Biome with an SDK-bundled fallback for pre-install generation): the extension `config.json` (`trim-extensions.ts`), the page-designer static registry (`staticRegistry.ts`), and cartridge metadata (`generate-cartridge.ts`). This keeps a freshly generated project lint-clean out of the box and stops the generated files churning on `biome format --write`. The template mirror script writes standalone `.oxlintrc.json` + `biome.json` (merged to `root: true`) and ships the custom OxLint plugins.

- #2454 `959a001` Thanks @harshini-magesh_sfemu! - Fix the mini-cart approaching-discounts banner going stale after a quantity or remove change. A basket mutation publishes a down-shaped response (mutations cannot send `expand=approaching_discounts`) while the expanded re-fetch publishes the same revision with `approachingDiscounts` populated; the provider's `lastModified` dedup dropped whichever landed second, so the banner could not re-render until a full page reload. `useBasketUpdater` now applies a shape-aware tie-break: a same-revision write that adds `approachingDiscounts` upgrades the context basket instead of being deduped away, while strictly-older revisions are still skipped (stale-clobber protection unchanged).

- #2481 `999018c` Thanks @jcesarpierre_sfemu! - Remove Storybook docs and config references to commands and options unavailable in a generated project

- #2270 `036c9cb` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Fix a11y: wrap grouped form fields in checkout (contact info, shipping address, credit card, billing address) in `<fieldset>` with an `sr-only` `<legend>` (WCAG 1.3.1). Also restructure shipping-method radio buttons so `<RadioGroupItem>` is not nested inside `<label>`; use `aria-labelledby` instead. Previously NVDA announced each radio as "1 of 1" instead of "1 of N".

- #2272 `9e49322` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Fix a11y: move keyboard focus in checkout when it would otherwise be lost. (1) When Place Order is clicked with invalid payment fields, focus moves to the first invalid field instead of staying on the Place Order button (WCAG 2.4.3). (2) When a shopper edits a completed section and clicks Continue, focus moves to the just-saved section's title after it collapses, instead of being dropped to `<body>` (WCAG 2.4.3).

- #2267 `5684845` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Fix a11y in checkout forms: use descriptive label "Expiry Date" for the credit card expiry field (WCAG 2.4.6) and set `autoComplete` to a sectioned token like `"shipping street-address"` or `"billing street-address"` on Address Line 1 instead of `off` (WCAG 1.3.5). Address Line 1 previously blocked browser autofill; the fix restores autofill for a personal-data field.

- #2266 `11322c7` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Fix a11y: mark checkout section titles ("Contact Information", "Shipping Address", "Shipping Method", "Payment") as `<h2>` headings instead of `<span>` (WCAG 1.3.1). Screen reader users can now navigate the checkout page by heading.

- #2269 `6d755de` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Fix a11y: add an `aria-live="polite"` status region on the checkout page that announces "Saving" during section submits and "Placing order" during the Place Order flow. Previously JAWS and NVDA users received no feedback while the loading spinner was on screen. WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA).

- #2268 `8eb674c` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Fix a11y: mark up Order Summary cost breakdown as a description list (`<dl>`/`<dt>`/`<dd>`) and product variant attributes as an unordered list (`<ul>`/`<li>`). Screen readers now announce the key/value relationship and list structure. WCAG 1.3.1.

- #2327 `6616f5b` Thanks @s-hussain_sfemu! - Enable the full `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` recommended rule set (plus `no-aria-hidden-on-focusable` and `anchor-ambiguous-text`) so accessibility defects are caught at lint time. A few intentional patterns (autofocus on section open, arrow-key navigation within swatch and option groups, the labelled carousel region, and Page Designer edit-mode drag handles) keep scoped inline disables and change no runtime behavior.

  Pins `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y>minimatch` to `3.1.2` via `pnpm.overrides`. The plugin's rule resolution (notably `label-has-associated-control`) depends on minimatch v3 glob semantics; a transitive bump to v10 changes brace/negation handling and silently breaks that rule. Keep this pin until the plugin declares v10 support — do not remove it in a routine dependency bump.

When account creation on the order confirmation fails, the error message receives focus and is announced to screen readers.

- #1999 `5a0ef18` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - perf(revalidation): skip checkout-loader revalidation on step submissions

  Add an intent-based denylist to the checkout route's `shouldRevalidate` policy so the loader does not re-run after step submissions (`contactInfo`, `shippingAddress`, `shippingOptions`, `payment`). Each step action already returns the updated basket in its JSON response and the form page applies it directly via `updateBasket(fetcher.data.basket)`; the loader re-run was redundant SCAPI traffic that roughly doubled the cost of every step submission.

  The pre-existing 3xx-redirect skip and the `framework_skipRevalidation` extension opt-in are preserved unchanged. The policy is moved from inline in `_checkout.checkout.tsx` into `src/lib/routes/revalidation/checkout.ts` for testability and to cluster per-route revalidation policies in one place, matching the pattern established by the root-route policy.

- #1884 `b6c83fb` Thanks @jcesarpierre_sfemu! - Restore Header snapshot coverage by stubbing <Await> in the snapshot harness

- #2347 `612c12c` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Render the tracking-consent banner client-only and gate it on the `dw_dnt` cookie. The banner no longer emits any node during SSR, and `dw_dnt` is now served as a non-httpOnly cookie so the client can decide whether to show the banner. This prevents app-shell caching from freezing consent state across shoppers. The consent write flow (server action + SLAS token refresh) is unchanged, and the JWT `dnt` claim remains the source of truth.

A card with no image, text, or button still renders nothing visible.

- #2372 `b116715` Thanks @daniel-diaz_sfemu! - Add selectable title and description typography presets to Content Card in Page Designer. The default preserves the existing look, so untouched cards are unchanged; editorial pages can now pick a shared typography preset instead of per-instance styling overrides.

  The cosmetic About Us cards were migrated from per-instance `className` overrides to these presets. Because the presets come from the shared (non-responsive) `typographyVariants` scale, those cards' mobile and `md:` sizes shift slightly to the standardized scale by design — this is the intended tradeoff of a single shared source of truth over one-off responsive hacks.

- #2121 `1ebda6f` Thanks @cboscenco_sfemu! - Add a cosmetic-vertical override of the bonus-product carousel that turns each tile's CTA into a 3-state toggle: **Pick** (adds the bonus product) → **Adding…** (this tile's request in flight) → **Selected** (removes it from the basket). Clicking a Selected tile now removes the line item, so shoppers can deselect a bonus product directly from the carousel.

  Each tile owns its own fetcher, so only the clicked tile shows the pending label instead of every tile flashing "Adding…". In-flight adds count toward the promotion's max (optimistic max), disabling the remaining unselected tiles immediately while selected tiles stay enabled so they can be toggled off. Selection is derived from the live basket, so a failed over-max add needs no manual rollback — the tile resolves back to "Pick" and an error toast fires. A successful remove (which returns a bare basket) no longer triggers a spurious error toast.

  Redesigns the cosmetic tile: a compact `w-32` card laid out as image → title → subtitle → CTA, presented in a simple horizontal scroll-snap rail (no carousel arrows). Drops the "Free" badge and strikethrough price. The image carries two overlays — a round checkmark badge (top-right) when the product is selected, colored like the selected CTA, and an optional uppercase product badge (top-left, e.g. Sale/New from the shared product-badge config) styled with the secondary token. The subtitle shows a configurable variation attribute's value display name (default `size`, e.g. "10 ml, 1 week supply"), falling back to the product short description and omitting cleanly when neither is present.

  The rail title shows the promotion's shopper-facing call-out message (paired with a gift icon); the promotion `name` is never shown, since it is the admin/Business-Manager label and is often just the promotion id. The cart loader now also resolves promotions from the basket's `bonusDiscountLineItems` (not only from product price adjustments), so a choice-of-bonus promotion's call-out is available even before any bonus product is selected and at max — the title shows the real message instead of the generic "Bonus Products Available" fallback. Once the promotion's bonus-product limit is reached, the title icon swaps from the gift to a sparkles icon, the "n/m" selection count is hidden, and a notice renders under the rail — a "Free" badge (soft primary tint) followed by a confirmation message. These are gated on the basket-confirmed selection count (not the optimistic in-flight count) so a failed over-max add cannot flash them in and out. While an add is in flight the tile shows "Adding…"; removing a selected tile shows "Removing…".

  Scoped to the cosmetic vertical. The canonical bonus-product component gains one optional, unused `promotion` prop (so the cart can pass the raw promotion `name`/`calloutMsg` through to vertical overrides) — fashion behavior is unchanged. Canonical locales and i18n types are untouched; the new cosmetic CTA/notice labels live in the cosmetic locale overrides via the i18next default-value form, and the subtitle variation-attribute id is configurable via the cosmetic UI config.

- #2033 `2d8baef` Thanks @daniel-diaz_sfemu! - Align the cosmetic vertical's visual design with the Dazzle reference. Replaces the dropped Glow & Co direction (pink/mauve) with Dazzle's sage + cream + warm-beige palette across every token file, and brings borders, shadows, and corner radii to pixel parity. Highlights: byte-aligned color tokens (oklch), `--ui-radius`/`--ui-shadow` shape tokens written to the source vars (not the inlined `@theme` bridge), a `tokens/sidebar.css` for account-nav hover, wider `max-w-[1680px]` editorial container, borderless cards on home/PLP/PDP with delineation borders restored on account/auth/checkout/order-confirmation, a smooth scroll-to-solid header transition with no layout shift, a seamless mega-menu dropdown (squared top corners, single hairline), unified nav-item hover, and a single mini-cart close button. Also adds a `storybook:test:mirror` script that validates a vertical's Storybook snapshots against the flattened mirror output the way CI does (avoiding false failures from running snapshots against the unflattened source tree).

The DAL rewrite no longer carries a per-site `alias`, `name`, or top-level `domain`. Routing derives each resolved site's `alias` from the static `siteAliasMap` and its `name` from the site `id`, so those DAL fields were overwritten before routing read them. - #2090 `2c96a51` Thanks @jbisa_sfemu! - fix(checkout): keep shopper on Shipping Address after refresh when no valid shipping methods are available for the entered address

- #2096 `89c07df` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - fix(checkout): place the order reliably after the payment fetcher resolves

  When a new card had to be synced before placing the order, the effect that chains place-order off the payment fetcher keyed on `paymentFetcher.state === 'idle'`. A fetcher reads `idle` both before its submission starts and after it completes, so the check could not distinguish "payment not submitted yet" from "payment finished". React Router 7.18 defers fetcher state updates, so a render now runs while the fetcher is still idle right after submit; the effect read that pre-submission idle tick as a payment failure and cleared the place-order intent before the request even left the browser. The order was then never placed and the shopper sat on the checkout page. The effect now reacts only to the fetcher transitioning into idle (it was in flight and just resolved), so the place-order step fires exactly once on real payment success.

When no realm can be derived, `replaceImageFormat` and `getSrc` now correctly skip format conversion and DIS param injection (`sw`, `sh`, `q`, `sfrm`).

The coupon-remove spec no longer calls `selectAllVariants()`, which navigated off the only variant `5ties` discounts and left the coupon unapplicable (no badge, timeout). The `add first address` spec now asserts the named address card is present after refresh instead of a visible count of 1: the card wrapper and its inner name are separate React renders, so right after the refresh's revalidation `getAddressCount()` sporadically read 0 while the name node — the one `waitForAddressWithName()` waits on — was already attached.

- #2273 `1dbb367` Thanks @emmyzhang_sfemu! - Fix external Page Designer content links that were entered without a URL scheme. `buildUrl` now recognizes explicit schemes (`mailto:`, `tel:`, `https:`, etc.) and normalizes scheme-less bare domains (e.g. `www.google.com`) to `https://`, so they navigate to the external site instead of being mangled into a site-prefixed internal path like `/global/en-GBwww.google.com`.

- #2196 `1503ac0` Thanks @sprasoon_sfemu! - Harden carrier tracking-link handling against three edge cases.
  - **Open-redirect via leading whitespace/control chars.** A tracking URL with leading whitespace or control characters around a relative path (e.g. `" /\x00/evil.com"`) previously skipped the relative-path guard and, once the control characters were stripped, collapsed into a protocol-relative `//host` that was rewritten into an absolute external link to an attacker-controlled host. The relative-path guard now runs on the leading-trimmed input before control characters are stripped, so such payloads are rejected; genuine scheme-less and protocol-relative values with surrounding whitespace continue to resolve normally.
  - **Internal-network redirect via private/reserved IPs.** A tracking URL pointing at a loopback, link-local, RFC 1918, or otherwise non-public IPv4 literal (`127.0.0.1`, `169.254.169.254`, `192.168.x.x`, `10.x`, `172.16-31.x`, …) was treated as a valid external host. Such hosts are now rejected so a tracking link can't be pointed at the storefront's own network; public IPv4 hosts still resolve.
  - **Empty tracking card from blank fields.** A whitespace-only tracking field returned by the order-management source was truthy and produced an empty tracking card or a "Track shipment" action that linked nowhere. Blank/whitespace-only shipment fields are now normalized to unset, so such entries are dropped instead of rendered.

- #2180 `e547cd5` Thanks @jcesarpierre_sfemu! - Regenerate the stale Footer signup snapshot (`InvalidEmailValidation`) so its button radius matches the `rounded-ui` shape token.

- #2198 `4ddec8c` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Fix guest checkout email persisting on the order and order confirmation after signing in with a different email. When a shopper enters an email at contact-info as a guest and then signs in (via passwordless OTP or standard email/password) with a different email, the basket's `customerInfo.email` is now reconciled to the signed-in customer's email before the order is placed. Reconciliation is applied in two layers: (1) the checkout loader guards re-check email identity on every revalidation and call `updateCustomerForBasket` when the basket email differs from the authenticated customer's email; (2) the OTP and standard-login actions perform the same reconciliation server-side immediately after sign-in, so the fix does not depend on a follow-up revalidation. Reconciliation failures log and continue - the loader guard is the safety net.

  Also fix a related case where editing the contact-info email and then dismissing the sign-in prompt via "proceed as guest" left the old email on the basket. The proceed-as-guest paths (both the standard login modal and the passwordless OTP modal) now submit the newly-typed email through the normal contact-info path before continuing, so the contact summary and the basket reflect the new email.

- #1941 `4987fd3` Thanks @vcua_sfemu! - Fix products with no price for the active currency showing as free and remaining purchasable. When a currency has no price-book entry, SCAPI omits the price field; the storefront previously treated that as `0`, so such products displayed as "$0.00" and could still be added to cart and checked out. Purchasability now requires a price for the active currency (an explicit price of `0` is still purchasable), and the price area shows "Price unavailable" instead of a misleading 0 on catalog surfaces (PLP, PDP, tiles). Promotional bonus products, which are intentionally free, are unaffected.

- #2023 `37d9aee` Thanks @kevin-he_sfemu! - Stop marking cookies `Secure` in local development so Safari can persist them. The template's `getCookieConfig` (auth, basket, shopper-context, turnstile cookies) hardcoded `secure: true`, and the SDK's site-context cookies (`site_id`, `lng`, `currency`) gated `secure` on `NODE_ENV`. Both now gate on a new shared `isRemote()` helper (`@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/env`, the `BUNDLE_ID` signal) — `true` on deployed Managed Runtime (HTTPS), `false` on local `pnpm dev` and `pnpm preview`.

  Previously, on `http://localhost` Safari/WebKit silently refused to persist `Secure` cookies (Chrome and Firefox mask this with a localhost exception), so no auth cookie ever stuck — sign-in and registration redirected straight back to a guest session. `NODE_ENV` was the wrong signal because `pnpm preview` runs a production build over plain HTTP; `BUNDLE_ID` is the same signal that already gates HSTS and `upgrade-insecure-requests`, so cookies, HSTS, and CSP now agree on "is this real HTTPS?". `SameSite=None` cookies (Page Designer design mode) stay `Secure` regardless, as the spec requires. `isRemote()` is also now exported from the SDK and the security-headers middleware consumes it instead of its own private copy.

- #2111 `6eb1235` Thanks @daniel-diaz_sfemu! - Fix the flaky `Storybook Tests` static a11y/interaction step. The harness used `npx serve` to host the static build, which resolved the `serve` package from the network on every run (it wasn't a dependency) and intermittently blew past the readiness window under CI load — surfacing only as a bare `wait-on ... Timed out waiting for http://127.0.0.1:3000` with no diagnostics. Pin `serve` as a devDependency and invoke it (and `wait-on`) via the local binary, buffer the server's output so a real startup failure is printed instead of swallowed, and detect early server-exit so it fails fast instead of waiting the full timeout.

- #2003 `26bacc1` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Fix hybrid (SFRA/SiteGenesis) handoff to the legacy backend.

  `hybrid.legacyRoutes` entries now accept an optional per-route `suffix` (e.g. `{ pattern: '/product/:id', suffix: '.html' }`) so legacy SEO URLs resolve. Bare-string entries are unchanged and never get a suffix, so clean-path routes like `/cart` stay clean.

  The site-aware `<Link>` now detects legacy routes and performs a full-document navigation (`reloadDocument`) — with the configured suffix applied — instead of relying on the client-side redirect middleware. The middleware-only approach raced React Router's own failed-chunk reload and silently stranded Safari on the current page (e.g. clicking the logo on the cart page did nothing). Handling the handoff at the link level means React Router never starts a client navigation to a legacy route, fixing the cross-browser inconsistency. The middleware remains as a backstop for programmatic `navigate()` calls.

  Removed the `redirected=1` loop-guard query param the middleware previously appended to the redirect URL. It was a PWA Kit holdover (that app's client router re-ran on every load); in this SSR app React Router does not run client middleware on the initial document load, so the loop it guarded against cannot occur. The param leaked to the legacy backend, whose SEO URL rules 404'd on it (e.g. `/category/kitchen?redirected=1`). Redirects now hand the legacy backend a clean URL.

  The legacy-routes middleware now skips Storefront Next infrastructure paths (`/resource/*`, `/action/*`, `/mobify/*`, `/assets/*`, `*.data`, and static assets) before matching. React Router runs client middleware for data/fetcher loads, not just navigations, so a path like `/resource/basket-products` was reaching the matcher; with a `'/:siteId/:localeId'` URL prefix it stripped down to `/`, and when `/` is a configured legacy route the fetcher load triggered a full-page navigation to the legacy backend — bouncing the shopper off Storefront Next with no click. The skip-list mirrors the dev proxy's exclusions and the infrastructure patterns in the eCDN routing rules.
