- #1962 `ad013de` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - fix(login): auto-submit the OTP code on fill and stop the input boxes overflowing the modal

  Two corrections to the OTP verification modal, both surfaced from the checkout flow:
  - **Auto-submit restored.** The modal again submits as soon as the visible slots are completely filled — typed or pasted — instead of requiring a separate **Verify** button click. This matches the checkout UX the modal was originally specified to (one fewer step to log in). Submission fires when the entered code exactly fills the visible slot count, so it never sends a short prefix of a still-being-typed longer code; a code pasted longer than the configured length still expands the boxes and submits whole. The Verify button is removed.
  - **Box overflow fixed.** Each slot was a fixed 48px wide, so an 8-slot row (an 8-digit OTP length) ran past the dialog's right edge — the boxes were clipped on the checkout modal. The slots are now capped at the same design width but shrink to fit, so a full 8-box row stays inside the modal at every viewport. (The overflow predated this change; it was only visible once an OTP length produced 8 boxes.)

  The OTP length itself is delivered by SLAS, not the storefront — `config.auth.otpLength` is only the storefront's guess and can drift from what SLAS sends. Aligning the configured length with the SLAS-issued length is tracked separately with the SLAS team.

- #1903 `f50c8d6` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - fix(login): tolerate an OTP length mismatch at the verification modal

  `config.auth.otpLength` is the storefront's configured guess at the OTP length, but SLAS owns the length it actually delivers (it emails the code straight to the shopper — the request contract carries no length field), so the two can drift. Previously the modal rendered exactly `otpLength` single-digit slots and only submitted once all of them filled, so a client whose SLAS OTP is longer than the configured length stranded the shopper: they physically could not enter the extra digits.

  The modal now degrades gracefully across the 6–8 digit range SLAS issues:
  - It renders `otpLength` slots by default but **expands to fit a longer pasted code**, up to the 8-digit SLAS maximum — so the box count matches the code the shopper actually received (6 boxes for a 6-digit code, 8 for an 8-digit one).
  - A typed code submits via an explicit **Verify** button (enabled at 6–8 gapless digits); a **pasted** code auto-submits, since a paste arrives whole and can't be a prefix of a longer code.

  The default `otpLength` stays **6** (unchanged from `main`).

  **Why it's built this way:**
  - _Default stays 6._ Six digits is the industry norm and product's intended default; new SLAS clients move to 6-digit during the Fast Storefront setup work, so the storefront default and SLAS converge on 6. This change does not touch the default — it makes the modal resilient to the transitional period (and any future drift) where a client's SLAS OTP length doesn't match the configured value.
  - _Expand on paste, not "always render 8."_ The storefront cannot know the delivered length ahead of time, so it cannot pre-render the correct number of boxes. Always rendering 8 would leave two permanently-empty boxes for every 6-digit shopper and contradict the "we sent a 6-digit code" copy. Growing to fit the pasted code keeps the box count honest and the common case clean.
  - _Auto-submit on paste only, not on type._ Auto-submitting the moment a **typed** code hits the configured length would fire a 6-digit prefix of a longer code before the shopper finished — re-creating the block as a rejection loop, because a typed code's final length is unknowable mid-entry. A **paste** has no such ambiguity (it arrives whole), so a pasted 6-to-8-digit code auto-submits; typed codes confirm with Verify.
  - _Known limitation (by design):_ a code longer than `otpLength` that is **typed by hand** rather than pasted won't expand the inputs — auto-growing on each keystroke would show a spurious empty box to every correctly-configured shopper, a worse regression than the gap. OTPs are nearly always pasted/autofilled; the shopper can also paste or correct the config.

  Also removes the unused `react-hook-form`/`zod` scaffolding from the modal (it was never wired to submission) and the orphaned `login.otpRequired` / `login.otpInvalidFormat` strings.

- #2458 `5fe6cb1` Thanks @jangho-jung_sfemu! - Address passkey PR review feedback. Consolidate the duplicate SDK passkey registration surface: widen `auth.webAuthn.authorizeRegistration`/`startRegistration`/`finishRegistration` to work with either a public or private SLAS client (the client secret is now optional, and the `Authorization` Basic-auth header is only sent when a secret is configured), and remove the redundant unreleased `auth.passkey` namespace in favor of `auth.webAuthn`. Gate the seven passkey server routes on `features.passkey.enabled` so they return `404` when the feature is disabled. Add a `parseRequestOptionsFromJSON` capability gate to the passkey login hook and drop the unsafe raw cast so unsupported browsers no longer attempt the ceremony. Surface post-gesture finish failures through a new `onError` channel on `usePasskeyLogin`, wired on both the login page and the checkout contact-info step. Add the missing `account.passkeys` locale keys (`loadError`, `nameTooLong`, `unsupportedBrowser`) and split the flat `uses` key into `uses_one`/`uses_other` plural forms. Per the team convention, all `account.passkeys` strings this feature introduced now reuse the English copy across the non-English locale files, letting them fall back to English until an official translation pass is done rather than shipping self-authored translations. Extract the base64url encoder into a shared `bufferToBase64Url` in `lib/auth/webauthn` so the login assertion path and the registration attestation fallback (browsers lacking `PublicKeyCredential.toJSON`) encode byte-for-byte identically. Bail silently in the login hook when no configured RP ID matches the current hostname, since passing the raw comma-separated list to the WebAuthn API would throw pre-gesture. Add a `405` method guard to the finish-authentication route. Handle the `412` SLAS response on start-authentication as a benign ~1-minute re-attempt throttle by returning silently (mirroring PWA Kit), rather than surfacing it as a `429` "Too many attempts" error. Fix the checkout `LoginModal` password/passwordless login when passkeys are enabled: the modal detects success by watching its fetcher return to idle, but the login action's `redirectDocument` (used to dismiss a lingering passkey picker) unmounts the modal before `onSuccess` fires, so the checkout step never advances and the page hard-reloads. The modal now submits `skipDocumentRedirect` to force the client-side `redirect`, matching the account re-auth path.

- #2161 `93eb6f2` Thanks @daniel-diaz_sfemu! - Remove the UITarget development overlay and its smoke-test harness. These were internal-only debugging aids that could cause build failures when trimming extensions.

If your project imports this plugin, remove the `uiTargetDevMode()` call from your `vite.config.ts` and delete any `vite-plugins/ui-target-dev-mode.ts` wrapper file. The export will be removed in v2.

- #2329 `b97e72b` Thanks @emmyzhang_sfemu! - Remove the move and delete handles from the root component on the Page Designer design-mode canvas. When editing a single content block in the focused visual canvas (the `preview/component` route), the block can no longer be moved or deleted from its canvas toolbar — it stays selectable and configurable, and its nested children keep their own handles. Implemented via a new opt-in `RootComponentProvider` (from `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/design/react/core`) that the preview route wraps around the previewed component; the design decorators read it to suppress the root's move/delete affordances. No effect at runtime or when the provider is absent.

- #2361 `70683a7` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Sweep residual SBOM advisories: exact-pin `lodash-es@4.18.1`, `joi@17: 17.13.4`, `js-yaml@3: 3.15.0`, `nanoid@3: 3.3.8`, `form-data@4: 4.0.6`, and `@opentelemetry/core@2: 2.8.0` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and mirror in `packages/template/package.json`. Per-major scoping (`pkg@N: X.Y.Z`) keeps sibling majors — the existing `joi@18`/`js-yaml@4`/`uuid@11` pins and OTEL 1.x — untouched. Documented accepted exceptions: `uuid@3.4.0` and `uuid@8.3.2` (no in-major fix; only 9.0.0+), `@opentelemetry/core@1.30.1` (no 1.x fix; SDK-wide 2.x migration deferred), and `diff@7.0.0` (no in-7.x fix).

- #1869 `592b2b6` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Format the generated page-designer static registry with the project's Prettier config so it is no longer reformatted on every commit. Previously the generator emitted trailing whitespace and over-width `registerImporter` lines, so a standalone `prettier --write` rewrote the file on every commit. The generated file is now also exempted in the ESLint config alongside other generated artifacts, and the redundant `/* eslint-disable */` it used to emit is dropped.

- #2246 `b4652dc` Thanks @jcesarpierre_sfemu! - Add Storybook coverage for My Cart single-item and empty-basket states, Account Overview quick links and rate-purchases card, and Product Grid pickup availability. Test-only — no component behavior changes.

- #2344 `fba98df` Thanks @jcesarpierre_sfemu! - Reorganize the Storybook sidebar into a consistent, domain-based component taxonomy

- #2339 `8d4efdf` Thanks @jcesarpierre_sfemu! - Document the Storybook test-runner workflow in README-STORYBOOK.md (two-engine split, local Playwright prerequisite, CI execution).

- #2274 `53acac4` Thanks @s-mahajan_sfemu! - Stream the checkout page's registered-shopper prefill and shipping-methods lookups instead of awaiting them in the loader. First byte no longer blocks on the ECOM `sfcc.app.shipping.calculate` hook (which makes outbound HTTP calls when a shipping app like CDS is installed on every prefill mutation). The page shell — title, express payments, contact info, order summary, my cart — renders eagerly; only the shipping-address / shipping-options section suspends on the streamed methods map, and the streamed prefill result is republished into the shared basket provider via a dedicated `PrefillSync` Suspense boundary.

  Hardens the streamed prefill against two edge cases: (1) attaches `.catch()` handlers to the streamed prefill and shipping-methods promises so a rejected lookup degrades to the loader basket / an empty methods map instead of throwing into the checkout error boundary (fail-open); (2) gates the returning-shopper Place Order / Payment section on `shippingMethodsResolved` so it stays hidden until the streamed methods map lands, preventing a brief PLACE_ORDER → Shipping Address flash when a saved address turns out to be undeliverable.

  Also fixes checkout progression requiring a second Continue click after entering an address or selecting a shipping method.

- #1984 `6b2c945` Thanks @vmarta_sfemu! - Pass `--coverage` to `vitest run` in the template's `pnpm test` script so the coverage thresholds defined in `vitest.config.ts` are actually enforced when the script runs in CI. Without the flag Vitest skipped the coverage pass entirely, leaving the configured thresholds (`{ lines: 73, statements: 73, functions: 72, branches: 67 }`) unchecked on every PR.

- #2179 `a28a3b6` Thanks @jcesarpierre_sfemu! - Add `Theme/*` design-token Storybook stories (Colors, Typography, Radius, Shadows). These render the active vertical's design tokens live (no hard-coded values) as a visual-regression baseline for the design system.

- #2078 `18613f7` Thanks @sprasoon_sfemu! - Hide the "Track shipment" action instead of linking to a tracking section that will not render. When the only tracking entry has a carrier URL that cannot be turned into a safe external link (and no tracking number, provider, or delivery date), the order details page no longer shows a "Track shipment" link that scrolls to an absent section.

- #2078 `18613f7` Thanks @sprasoon_sfemu! - Harden carrier tracking-link normalization against host-confusion. A tracking URL shaped `label.tld://host/path` is now rejected instead of being rewritten into a link that reads like one host but navigates to another; genuine scheme-less `host:port` values continue to resolve normally.

- #1936 `6e98953` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Fix two checkout Turnstile optimizations:
  - Stop rendering a second Turnstile widget at the "Save for Future Use" step; rely on the server-side `cc-tv` cookie short-circuit in `enforceTurnstile` so subsequent Turnstile-protected actions in the same checkout flow skip re-verification
  - Gate the Continue button on contact-info on `form.formState.isValid` so an incomplete form cannot be submitted, and remove the misleading "verification refreshed" toast on Turnstile timeout (Cloudflare auto-refreshes silently)

- #2271 `695fea7` Thanks @jcesarpierre_sfemu! - Add design-system Storybook stories for the UI primitives (Button, Input, Dialog, Form) as multi-state galleries under the `UI/*` group, and opt the design-system layer (the new UI galleries plus `Theme/Colors`) into Chromatic visual testing via the `chromatic-core` tag.

- #2367 `b09690d` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Fix `QuickAddButton` keeping its quick-add modal mounted forever after the first open. The modal was gated on a sticky `loaded` latch that never reset, so the modal's `useScapiFetcher` product fetchers stayed registered in the fetcher registry after close and were re-run on every subsequent context mutation (currency/locale/site switch, store selection). The modal now gates on `open` via a new `useDeferredUnmount` hook that keeps it mounted briefly after close so the Radix exit animation plays, then unmounts it so the fetchers deregister.

- #2393 `d706339` Thanks @emmyzhang_sfemu! - Fix mini-PD content block editor: components rendered permanently selected/unclickable. Fall back to the component `id` when a block has no `contentLinkUuid` so selection/hover identity is never the empty string (which collided with the empty-string selection default).

  Also fix the design frame's name label being clipped when a component sits flush to the top of the canvas (as in the content block editor): the label now renders inside the top edge instead of above it when there isn't room.

- #2328 `98b3c41` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Remove the residual per-page-view wishlist `productLists` SCAPI read. Loaders no longer fetch wishlist state on every page view; the client store fills hearts lazily on the shopper's first product intent (tile hover / PDP heart mount) by calling a new GET-only resource route, `/action/wishlist-state`, once per session. The route is read-only (`getWishlist`, never `getOrCreateWishlist`), works for any session with a valid `customerId` (guest or registered), and is best-effort — any failure resolves to unfilled hearts rather than breaking browse. Every response is served `Cache-Control: no-store`, since the body is a per-shopper read from a fixed, query-less URL that a cache would otherwise key under one shopper for all. This eliminates the wishlist read from the hot routes (home, PLP, PDP, search, cart, account overview) for both guest and registered sessions.

- #2199 `84ce79b` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Stop wishlist hydration from creating empty product lists on every page load. `fetchWishlistInitialState` now reads the wishlist (`getWishlist`) instead of get-or-create, so a shopper with no wishlist yet hydrates to an empty product set without a `POST` create, an index-propagation sleep, and a re-read. The list is provisioned lazily on the shopper's first add, which the `WishlistProvider` routes through the `/action/wishlist-add` server action (add and remove both run entirely server-side). Wishlist write requests are serialized so the first add finishes creating the list before any later write runs, preventing duplicate lists when a shopper adds several products in quick succession. This removes the dominant source of `customers/product-lists` SCAPI traffic — and of orphaned empty lists — observed during scale/load tests, which was driven by guest sessions hitting the hot routes (home, PLP, PDP, search, cart, account overview).

- #2060 `3ed5c33` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Tighten the `/wishlist` and `/account/wishlist` `shouldRevalidate` gate to the ambient-mutations allowlist shared by the home route — the loader now re-runs only on `setSiteContext` (currency switch refreshes per-currency tile prices), `updateShopperContext` (cross-cutting input to every SCAPI response), and auth identity transitions (login / signup / logout re-seed the auth-dependent wishlist for the new identity). Add-to-cart from a wishlist tile, wishlist remove, payment changes, and account-preference mutations no longer re-fire `getCustomerProductLists` and the per-item product lookups for state the page doesn't render.

## 2026.7.0 (July 2026)

### Minor Changes

- #2140 `6b1a548` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Switch checkout revalidation from a boolean opt-out to tag-based opt-in; remove `FRAMEWORK_SKIP_REVALIDATION` export.

  The checkout route now declares `CHECKOUT_REVALIDATE_TAGS = ['checkout.update']` as its data-dependency vocabulary. Extension actions opt in to triggering a checkout-loader reload by returning `revalidateTags: ['checkout.update']` on their action result (or using the `withRevalidateTags` helper). An action that returns no matching tags skips the loader reload, so adoption is incremental - actions that previously used `framework_skipRevalidation: true` get the same "do not reload" behaviour automatically until they are updated.

  **Migration**: the `FRAMEWORK_SKIP_REVALIDATION` constant is no longer exported from `@/lib/revalidation/routes/checkout`. Remove any import of it and remove `framework_skipRevalidation: true` from action results. To suppress the checkout-loader reload, return a `revalidateTags` value that does not intersect with `CHECKOUT_REVALIDATE_TAGS` - for example `revalidateTags: ['checkout.payment.complete']`. To trigger a reload, include `'checkout.update'` in `revalidateTags`.

- #2185 `10e8454` Thanks @sprasoon_sfemu! - Add OMS shipment tracking to the Order Details page. When an order has Salesforce Order Management tracking data, each shipment shows the tracking number as a link to the carrier's tracking page, the carrier name, and the expected and actual delivery dates; a "Track shipment" action links straight to the carrier (or to the tracking section when no carrier link is available). Orders without OMS data continue to show the existing tracking number and status. The Order History list now also surfaces the OMS order status (the ECOM status is preferred, with the OMS status as a fallback).

  Carrier tracking-link normalization is hardened against host-confusion: a tracking URL shaped `label.tld://host/path` is rejected instead of being rewritten into a link that reads like one host but navigates to another; genuine scheme-less `host:port` values continue to resolve normally. When the only tracking entry has a carrier URL that cannot be turned into a safe external link (and no tracking number, provider, or delivery date), the "Track shipment" action is hidden rather than linking to a tracking section that will not render.

### Patch Changes

- #2260 `de109f2` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Fix DIS-eligibility check to anchor the `/dw/image/v2/` path match to `url.pathname` and gate it on a host-capability check.

  Previously the predicate tested the full URL string with an unanchored regex and never verified the host, so query strings, fragments, or third-party hosts carrying `/dw/image/v2/` in the path (e.g. `?ref=/dw/image/v2/foo`, `#/dw/image/v2/section`, `https://thirdparty.com/dw/image/v2/x.jpg`) were misclassified as DIS-eligible, received `sfrm`/`q`/`sw` parameters, and 404'd.

  Now a URL is DIS-eligible only when the `/dw/image/v2/` prefix appears at the start of the pathname **and** the host is DIS-capable — it matches `config.images.host`, a `config.images.realmHostMappings` entry, or a built-in SFCC domain (`.commercecloud.salesforce.com`, `.demandware.net`, `.my.cc.salesforce.com`). The `sfrm` marker is read from the parsed query string (in both `isDisTransformed` and `replaceImageFormat`), so a literal `&sfrm=` in a path segment no longer forces eligibility or short-circuits format conversion. The single-image `toImageUrl` fast path is gated on the same host-capability check, and the configured DIS host is parsed once and memoized. Vanity domains without a `realmHostMappings` entry now fail closed.

- #2261 `4c9a85b` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Fix `<DynamicImage>` so it only applies DIS transformation to URLs the imaging service can actually serve. With DIS enabled, the shared resolver keyed format conversion, quality, and `sw`/`sh` params off "is DIS enabled" — but a relative bundled asset (`/images/hero-01.webp`) or a non-SFCC host (`https://via.placeholder.com/300`) has no derivable realm, so `toDisBaseUrl` returns it unchanged and it never becomes a DIS URL. The resolver was still emitting a `<picture>` with dead `?sw=&q=` `<source>` variants and rewriting the `<img>` fallback to a non-existent path (`/images/hero-01.jpg?sfrm=webp` — a 404). It now derives `disApplies = enableDis && IS_DIS_URL_REGEX.test(transformedSrc)` and gates format conversion, quality, and the returned `enableDis` flag on it: relative and third-party URLs render verbatim in their own format with no conversion or query params, while a high-priority local image still emits a single `<link rel="preload">` so LCP heroes keep their preload hint. Genuine DIS-hosted SFCC URLs are unaffected.

- #2132 `7af1edb` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Fix the dev hybrid proxy to handle every `url.prefix` shape out of the box, so a locale-prefixed legacy path (e.g. `/uk/cart`) is no longer double-stacked into `/s/{siteId}/{locale}/uk/cart`.

  The dev proxy unconditionally prepended `/s/{defaultSiteId}/{locale}` to every non-SFRA path. Now that the template emits prefixed paths (`/uk/cart`, `/global/en-GB/cart`), that stacked the locale a second time and SFRA 404'd. The proxy now reads `app.url.prefix` and the site/locale alias catalog from `config.server.ts`, strips the prefix the URL already carries, and reuses that site/locale when decorating to SFRA's `/s/{siteId}/{locale}/…` shape — for no prefix, `/:localeId`, and `/:siteId/:localeId` alike. A captured segment is only treated as a site/locale when it is a known identifier, so a bare legacy path (`/cart` under `/:localeId`) isn't mistaken for a locale home. The root `/` maps to the locale-less SFRA site root and the query string is preserved across the rewrite.

  `hybridProxyPlugin` gains optional `urlPrefix`, `siteAliases`, `localeAliases`, and a last-resort `rewritePath` escape hatch for non-standard URL models. `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime` exports a new `extractPrefixParamValues` site-context helper (mirrors `stripPathPrefix`'s matching rules) that powers the prefix-aware rewrite.

- #2115 `eab5649` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Publish the updated basket revision from the bonus-product modal, bonus-product carousel direct-add, promo-code apply/remove, cart quantity-update, and cart-line remove handlers so `useBasket()` consumers (badge, mini-cart freshness reference) stay in sync after these mutations, matching the add/edit/remove handlers.

- #2222 `c016b62` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Add lazy data-store preference middleware and an opt-in cross-request L1 cache to cut DynamoDB reads on the single shared data-store partition

  The eager `dataStoreMiddleware` reads all four preference entries on every request that reaches root, even routes that never use them. All entries share one partition key (`"${MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID} ${DEPLOY_TARGET}"`), so that volume can throttle one physical partition under load.

  The new lazy variants (`customSitePreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, `customGlobalPreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, `gcpPreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, `loginPreferencesMiddlewareLazy`, their `get*Lazy` accessors, and the `dataStoreMiddlewareLazy` bundle) register a memoized loader instead of fetching up front, so the read fires only when a loader reads the value and repeat reads within a request share the promise. The eager exports are deprecated but unchanged. The template wires `dataStoreMiddlewareLazy`, reads login preferences via the async `getLoginPreferences` wrapper, and moves the GCP Address Autocomplete API key onto the checkout loader (the only route mounting `GoogleCloudApiProvider`).

  The L1 cache serves repeat reads of the same entry from memory. It lives on `globalThis` (via a `Symbol.for` key) to survive SSR module re-evaluation and persist across a warm Lambda's sequential requests. Only successful reads of deployment-/site-scoped preference entries are cached — never shopper data, fallbacks, missing entries, or errors; `getDataStoreEntry` stays a thin, cache-free read. It is off by default; set `MRT_DATA_STORE_CACHE_ENABLED=true` to opt in per environment (e.g. deployed MRT). `MRT_DATA_STORE_CACHE_TTL` sets the TTL in ms (default 300000) and `MRT_DATA_STORE_CACHE_MAXBYTES` the total-value byte budget (default 131072); zero/negative/non-numeric falls back to the default. The cache is bounded by byte size, not entry count, evicting least-recently-used keys. `clearDataStoreCache()` drops the instance for test isolation or to force-bust a warm container after a preference publish.

- #2144 `19beba8` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - perf(nav): fix whole-page hydration flicker caused by the mobile navigation drawer

  `MobileMenuDropdown` rendered its category list unconditionally and only hid it with CSS while the menu was closed. Each `MobileMenuCategory` subscribes to the sub-category store via `useSubCategory` (a `useSyncExternalStore` consumer), so those subscribers were present in the SSR/hydration tree even though the drawer was invisible. When the deferred sub-category promise resolved post-hydration and filled the store, the subscribers re-rendered, and because the header sits above `<Outlet/>` the re-render cascaded into a visible full-page flicker on every page.

  The drawer now mounts its subtree only while the menu is open, keeping the store subscribers out of the initial render. This matches the desktop mega panel, whose subscribers already live inside the lazily-mounted Radix content. No behavior change when the menu is open.

- #2145 `eadc14f` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - perf(wishlist): fix whole-page hydration flicker caused by WishlistProvider

  `WishlistProvider` deferred its SCAPI hydration to a post-mount `useEffect`, then wrote the resolved customer/list IDs into `useState` via `setHydrated`. That state update re-rendered the provider, which rebuilt the `useScapiFetchClient` add/remove hooks (the customer/list IDs were baked into their URLs at construction), changed the identities of the `add`/`remove`/`toggle` callbacks, produced a new `actions` value, and so changed the `WishlistActionsContext` value. Every `useWishlistActions` consumer in the page subtree re-rendered at once — a visible full-page flicker on every route that mounts a `WishlistProvider`.

  The provider no longer stores the customer/list IDs in React state. They live on a ref that the hydration effect updates without a re-render, and `add` supplies them per call via a `params` override (mirroring how `remove` already passed the item-keyed path). The `add`/`remove` dependency arrays shrink to `[store]`, so the `add`/`remove`/`toggle` callbacks stay referentially stable for the provider's lifetime and hydration no longer rebuilds them. Hydration still fills the store via `replaceAll`, which only re-renders the topic subscribers (heart icons) whose entries actually changed. No behavior change for guests or for the add/remove/toggle flows.

- #2256 `85cd00b` Thanks @vcua_sfemu! - w:

      Port the SCAPI 24-ID `getProducts` batching fix into the multi-vertical template
      (`packages/template/`) so it stays 1-1 with `template-retail-rsc-app`. The shared
      `fetchProductsByIds` helper now splits product IDs into batches of at most 24
      (SCAPI's `getProducts` limit), fetches them in parallel, and merges the results
 , and the remaining server-side callers — the checkout product map
      (`fetchProductsInBasket`), the mini-cart basket-products resource route, and the
      BOPIS pickup-store validation action — route through that helper so a basket or
      pickup with 25+ distinct products no longer trips `'ids' violates the value

  constraint. The expected value is between '(0..24)'` . The client-side
  bulk child-inventory hook still issues a single request (documented inline); a set
  or bundle with 25+ selected children remains a known limitation to batch separately.

- #2151 `3bd857d` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Refresh the checkout basket when the shopper returns to a tab they left open. When the basket is changed in another tab or device, returning to an open checkout tab now revalidates against the authoritative server basket instead of showing a stale cart total. The refresh skips while a navigation or fetcher submission is in flight, so it never interrupts mid-input, and does no work when the basket is unchanged.

- #2096 `89c07df` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - fix(checkout): place the order reliably after the payment fetcher resolves

  When a new card had to be synced before placing the order, the effect that chains place-order off the payment fetcher keyed on `paymentFetcher.state === 'idle'`. A fetcher reads `idle` both before its submission starts and after it completes, so the check could not distinguish "payment not submitted yet" from "payment finished". React Router 7.18 defers fetcher state updates, so a render now runs while the fetcher is still idle right after submit; the effect read that pre-submission idle tick as a payment failure and cleared the place-order intent before the request even left the browser. The order was then never placed and the shopper sat on the checkout page. The effect now reacts only to the fetcher transitioning into idle (it was in flight and just resolved), so the place-order step fires exactly once on real payment success.

- #2265 `52a9e96` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Add a `billingAddressGetter` field to `PaymentSubmissionRef`. Payment extensions that replace the `sfcc.checkout.payment` UI target and register `onPlaceOrder` can register this getter to hand the shopper's current billing address back to the checkout page; the checkout persists it to `basket.billingAddress` via a new `/resource/update-basket-billing-address` route before delegating to `onPlaceOrder`. The default form-based Payment component registers a getter that returns the currently-typed billing address when "billing differs" is checked and `null` otherwise, so existing storefronts see no behavior change.

- #2167 `7e805ba` Thanks @daniel-diaz_sfemu! - Drive corner radius from the `--ui-radius` shape token across more of the UI so roundness themes uniformly from a single source. Components that previously hardcoded their radius (e.g. `rounded-md`/`rounded-sm`) — the quantity picker, price-range inputs, color-filter swatches, promo-code chip, shipping calculator, store-availability filter, and order-confirmation thumbnails — now use the `rounded-ui` utility. Setting `--ui-radius` once themes all of them together (rounded or squared) without editing component source; full-pill elements opt in via `data-slot="badge"`.

- #2173 `24c55c2` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - When a registered shopper's access token refresh fails, redirect them to the login page with a session-expired message instead of silently downgrading to a guest session. Checkout shows an inline sign-in banner if a mid-checkout action fails with an unauthorized error.

- #2217 `9f58d28` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Stop wishlist hydration from creating empty product lists on every page load. `fetchWishlistInitialState` now reads the wishlist (`getWishlist`) instead of get-or-create, so a shopper with no wishlist yet hydrates to an empty product set without a `POST` create, an index-propagation sleep, and a re-read. The list is provisioned lazily on the shopper's first add, which the `WishlistProvider` routes through the `/action/wishlist-add` server action (add and remove both run entirely server-side). Wishlist write requests are serialized so the first add finishes creating the list before any later write runs, preventing duplicate lists when a shopper adds several products in quick succession. This removes the dominant source of `customers/product-lists` SCAPI traffic — and of orphaned empty lists — observed during scale/load tests, which was driven by guest sessions hitting the hot routes (home, PLP, PDP, search, cart, account overview).

- #1706 `7a4224b` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Move `<WishlistProvider>` from the global `_app.tsx` shell to route-local mounts via a new `<DeferredWishlistProvider>` helper. Routes that render wishlist UI (home, PDP, PLP, search, cart) hydrate their own provider via the loader; routes without wishlist UI (about-us, account/\* non-wishlist pages, order confirmation) no longer pay the SCAPI `getOrCreateWishlist` cost on cold load. `<WishlistMergeToast>` stays at the app shell.

- #1706 `7a4224b` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Add `useScapiFetchClient` / `useScapiFetchHelper` hooks and `<WishlistProvider>`: small UI mutations (e.g. PLP heart click) now hit a generic SCAPI resource route via `fetch` instead of `useFetcher`, so they no longer trigger React Router loader revalidation. Wishlist initial state is seeded once at the app shell behind `<Suspense>`/`<Await errorElement>`, so SCAPI failures still render the page 200 with empty hearts. Hydrates wishlists for both guest (gcid) and registered (rcid) sessions. Provider exposes topic-scoped subscription hooks (`useIsInWishlist`, `useWishlistEntry`, `useWishlistCount`, `useWishlistIds`, `useWishlistActions`) backed by `useSyncExternalStore` so a single heart toggle re-renders only that one tile, not every other heart in the grid

- #1823 `0a3fcdc` Thanks @arayanavarro_sfemu! - w:

  Tighten the `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/config` public surface for V1 GA.

  **Removed from public exports** (followups to #1741):
  - `ConfigContext` — internal React context backing `useConfig()`. Read config via `useConfig()` instead.
  - `createAppConfig` — one-line `.app` accessor with no semantic value. Use `staticConfig.app` directly.
  - The `middleware.ts` source file and `createAppConfigMiddleware` factory were also deleted; they had B2C-Commerce-specific validation hardcoded in (`commerce.api.{clientId,organizationId,shortCode}`, `SCAPI_PROXY_HOST`) and the retail template ships its own validating middleware. Future templates write their own.

  **Added** — `AppConfigShape` interface as a module-augmentation hook for `getConfig()` / `useConfig()` typing. Each template `declare module`s once in its own types file and gets typed access without the per-call `<AppConfig>` generic:

  ```ts
  // In your template's src/types/config.ts:
  declare module "@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/config" {
    interface AppConfigShape extends AppConfig {}
  }
  ```

  **Other changes**
  - `Locale`, `Site`, `Url` JSDoc reframed as opt-in baseline shapes — `BaseConfig<App>` is generic so future templates can ignore them.
  - `defineConfig` JSDoc now explicitly notes it reads `process.env` at call time (server-only side effect).
  - `mergeEnvConfig`'s engagement-specific protected-paths error message is now generic.
  - Retail-flavored examples in `schema.ts` / `utils.ts` JSDoc neutralized.
  - Template (`template-retail-rsc-app`): all 110+ `getConfig<AppConfig>()` / `useConfig<AppConfig>()` call sites now use the augmented hook (no per-call generic).
  - Template `commerce.sites: Site[]` now imports the richer `Site` shape from `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/site-context` (reconciles the duplicate `Site` types that existed across both subpaths).
  - `contact-info.tsx` migrated from `useContext(ConfigContext)` to `useConfig()` (the only production caller of the bypass pattern).
  - README-CONFIG.md fixed: `loadConfig` subpath was wrong (`/load-config` → `/config/load-config`); `appConfigContext` now documented for custom middleware composition; `AppConfigShape` augmentation pattern documented.

  Public surface delta: 13 runtime + 5 type exports → 5 + 6 (plus `loadConfig` at the separate `./config/load-config` subpath).

  > **Semver note for future maintainers:** This entry is a `minor` bump _only because the package is still pre-V1 GA_. Removing public exports is a `major` once V1 ships — do not paste this pattern after lock-in.

- #1836 `a5f5a3b` Thanks @alex-vuong_sfemu! - Make the SLAS access-token JWT the single source of truth for `userType`, alongside `customerId`, `usid`, and `accessTokenExpiry`. All four fields are now derived from the same JWT decode whenever a token response is written into the session, so they always travel together — there is no path where one drifts from the other.

  Fixes an in-request session-state bug where, immediately after a guest signed in (standard email/password, passwordless OTP, or social IDP), `session.customerId` kept the guest `gcid` for the rest of the request even though the registered access token carrying the correct `rcid` had already been persisted. Any in-request consumer that read `session.customerId` (basket merge, wishlist merge, anything pasting `customerId` into a SCAPI URL path) targeted the wrong customer. The bug self-healed on the next request because the auth middleware re-derived state from cookies before any handler ran.

  Internally:
  - `updateAuthStorageDataByTokenResponse` now derives `userType` from the JWT's `isb` claim (registered iff `rcid` is present and non-empty) and uses that value to cap the refresh-token expiry.
  - The four login sites (`standard-login.server.ts`, `_empty.login.tsx` passwordless auto-verify, `action.verify-passwordless-otp.ts`, `social-login.server.ts`) collapse from two `updateAuth(...)` calls to one.
  - The auth middleware's ingest path uses the JWT-derived `userType` whenever a decodable access token is present; cookie names (`cc-nx` / `cc-nx-g`) are now consulted only as a cold-start fallback when no access token has been issued yet, and as the response-side decision for which refresh-cookie to write or delete.
  - `getCustomerIdFromClaims` no longer takes a `userType` argument — it returns `rcid ?? gcid`, which is the right answer for either user type without disambiguation.

- #1840 `333e485` Thanks @alex-vuong_sfemu! - Restore guest wishlist support on the heart button. A guest clicking the heart now silently adds the item to their guest wishlist via the existing `WishlistProvider` and SCAPI's product-list endpoints (which accept guest gcid tokens). On sign-in, the existing `mergeWishlist` flow transfers the items to the registered account.

  The `WishlistButton` previously wrapped its toggle action with `useRequireAuth`, which redirected guests to `/login` before the provider's `add()` ever ran. The wrapper predated the rest of the guest-aware wishlist architecture (server-side hydration via `fetchWishlistInitialState`, action routes that explicitly support gcid tokens, the `/wishlist` guest route with its sign-in banner). Removing it lets the rest of the stack do the right thing for guests with no other changes.

  The component also drops the now-dead pending-action plumbing (`useCheckAndExecutePendingAction`, the URL-scrubbing `useEffect`, and the `pendingActionRef`/`wasPendingRef` refs) — those existed solely to support the post-login redirect-and-resume flow that no longer applies.

- #1848 `26a7f95` Thanks @clavery_sfemu! - Bump `@salesforce/b2c-tooling-sdk` to `^1.11.0` and `@salesforce/b2c-cli` to `^1.12.0` (latest published versions). - #1779 `8ae7030` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Stop the data-store middleware from crashing MRT requests on transient DAL failures. `DataStoreServiceError` and `DataStoreUnavailableError` now both honor `onUnavailable`, and the four built-in middlewares (`customSitePreferencesMiddleware`, `customGlobalPreferencesMiddleware`, `gcpPreferencesMiddleware`, `loginPreferencesMiddleware`) default to `'fallback'` so the request continues with the configured fallback value instead of throwing. `SFNEXT_DATA_STORE_UNAVAILABLE_MODE` is preserved as an opt-in escape hatch — set it to `'throw'` to restore fail-fast behavior. `DataStoreNotFoundError` keeps its existing missing-state semantics; errors thrown from `transform` still propagate. `createDataStoreMiddleware`'s factory default for customer-authored middlewares stays at `'throw'` (no change to the public API contract).

  Adds `dataStoreLoggerContext`, `getDataStoreLogger`, and the `DataStoreLogger` interface under `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/data-store`. Hosts can inject a request-scoped structured logger so SDK warnings emit with `correlationId`, `method`, and `path` bindings instead of bare `console.warn`. The storefront template's `loggingMiddleware` wires this automatically; when unset, falls back to a console-based logger that fail-soft serializes metadata (cyclic / unserializable values won't crash the request).

- #1924 `7850ace` Thanks @daniel-diaz_sfemu! - Fix account details email section buttons overflowing on mobile by adding flex-wrap so Verify Email and Change Email buttons wrap below the email address on narrow viewports

- #1767 `f94f6fe` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Fix auth callback URLs (social login, passwordless, password reset, SLAS `redirect_uri`) and SEO canonical/hreflang URLs on hybrid storefronts behind eCDN. These were built from `EXTERNAL_DOMAIN_NAME` (which resolves to the MRT-assigned host on hybrid deployments) instead of the customer's custom domain — social login redirected to the MRT host and 404'd, password-mode signup hit `redirect_uri doesn't match the registered redirects`, magic-link emails carried the wrong origin, and `<link rel="canonical">` / hreflang URLs pointed at the lambda-internal hostname.

  A new `requestOriginMiddleware` stashes the in-flight request in router context; `getAppOrigin(context)` lazily parses `x-forwarded-host` / `x-forwarded-proto` (with comma-split, leading-empty handling, and exact-match localhost detection) and memoizes per request. The SDK's host-header middleware already populates `x-forwarded-host` from `EXTERNAL_DOMAIN_NAME` when no upstream value is present, so a single deployment serves any custom domain without per-environment config. `createApiClients`, all auth-flow callbacks, the magic-link emailers, and `buildSeoMetaDescriptors` now resolve origin via context. `schema-url.ts` `getPublicOrigin` delegates to the same parser so JSON-LD URLs share the auth path's correctness fixes.

- #1806 `4f73f0e` Thanks @daniel-diaz_sfemu! - Fix BNPL target render loop on PDP. The previous implementation combined two deferred loader Promises with `Promise.all([...])` inside render, producing a fresh Promise on every render. React Router's `<Await>` tracks resolution by Promise identity, so each new Promise re-suspended and re-rendered in a microtask-fast loop — starving `useFetcher({ key: 'basket-products' })` of stable commit cycles (mini-cart never opened) and driving express-payments image churn. Each deferred Promise now gets its own `<Suspense>`/`<Await>` boundary so the loader's original Promise references flow through unchanged.

- #1948 `3535909` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Allow the OOTB Einstein engagement adapter through the default CSP. The adapter fires browser `navigator.sendBeacon` calls to the CQuotient activities API (`https://api.cquotient.com/v3/activities/...`), which is governed by `connect-src`. The default `connect-src` did not list that host, so every Einstein beacon (viewPage, viewProduct, viewCategory, …) was blocked by CSP and reported a console violation on a freshly generated project. Added `https://api.cquotient.com` to the default `connect-src` directive.

- #1939 `d273772` Thanks @arayanavarro_sfemu! - Fix three dev-server console errors in freshly generated projects (`pnpm dev`):
  - **Invalid hook call / "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext')"**: on first dev load Vite discovered the React-importing runtime SDK entry points (`/config`, `/security/react`, `/site-context`, `/design/react/core`, `/routing/app-wrapper`, `/i18n/client`) lazily at request time, triggering a dep re-optimization + full reload that transiently loaded a second React instance. Also pre-bundles the i18n peer deps the SDK imports internally but the template does not import from its own source (`i18next-browser-languagedetector`, used by `/i18n/client`; and `remix-i18next/middleware`, used by the SDK's `/i18n` barrel) — these are discovered late for the same reason. (`react-i18next` needs no entry: the template imports it directly, so Vite's initial source crawl already finds it.) All are now in the first-pass `optimizeDeps.include`, so a single optimization runs with one shared React and no mid-session reload.
  - **CSP blocked the Vite HMR websocket** (`ws://localhost:24678`): the security middleware now appends `ws://localhost:*`, `ws://127.0.0.1:*`, and `wss://localhost:*` to `connect-src` only when running locally (`BUNDLE_ID` unset or `local`). Deployed/MRT responses are unchanged.
  - **Nonce hydration mismatch** on the inline `window.__APP_CONFIG__` script: browsers strip the `nonce` content attribute from the DOM after applying CSP, so the client saw `nonce=""` against the server's real value. Added `suppressHydrationWarning` to that script element; the CSP nonce still applies.

- #1898 `dee3c0a` Thanks @mjuraschik_sfemu! - Fall back to category-level page assignment during manifest resolution when a product-keyed page lookup misses. `resolveDynamicPageId` and `resolvePage` now accept an optional `categoryId` (string or Promise) consulted only after the product lookup misses, and the Page Designer resolution middleware threads the request's categoryId through whenever a productId is also present.

- #1917 `51466d3` Thanks @vmarta_sfemu! - Make `en-GB` the authoritative locale for type-safe `t()` keys. Previously `en-GB` was the runtime fallback (`config.server.ts`) and the source the type augmentation read (`i18next.server.ts`), but every locale's `index.ts` — including `en-GB` itself — used `satisfies DeepPartial<typeof enUS>`, making `en-US` the compile-time root. The two only happened to agree because `en-GB` currently holds every key. This flips the `satisfies` chain to `DeepPartial<typeof enGB>` so the compile-time and runtime sources of truth match. No runtime behavior change.

- #1918 `bbb0926` Thanks @vmarta_sfemu! - Merge `product.json` back into `translations.json` for all 17 locales. The split was originally introduced to dodge a TypeScript compiler crash; with the locale tree settled, the merge now typechecks cleanly. Keeps a single canonical translations file per locale. The runtime backend still registers `product` as a top-level i18next namespace, so all `t('product:…')` and `useTranslation('product')` call sites are unaffected.

- #1909 `d7c73e1` Thanks @vmarta_sfemu! - Cut `pnpm lint` runtime by disabling `@typescript-eslint/no-misused-promises` `checksVoidReturn.attributes`. The sub-check scans every JSX event-handler attribute (`onClick`, `onChange`, …) against the value's return type, which fans out across thousands of TSX files and pushed `pnpm lint` past 30 minutes on customer 1x CI runners. The rule still fires on argument, property, return, and variable positions, so it continues to catch real misuse — only the JSX-attribute traversal is dropped.

- #1683 `fa0eca3` Thanks @vcua_sfemu! - Remove the redundant `customerId` auth cookie. `customerId` is now derived per-request from the SLAS access token JWT `isb` claim (via `gcid`/`rcid`) and continues to flow through `getAuth(context)` server-side and `useAuth()` client-side. The middleware no longer reads, writes, or actively clears the cookie — any value left in existing browsers is ignored and expires on its own. The `usid` cookie is **kept** — sf-next reads `usid` from the JWT `sub` claim, but the cookie is retained so hybrid storefronts can forward it to ECOM (which does not parse the access token for `usid`); the cookie value is also used as a cold-start fallback to preserve SLAS session continuity when no access token is present.

- #1678 `a54506a` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Rewrite extension descriptions in `src/extensions/config.json` to use "Enables" instead of "allows" (Salesforce style guide reserves "allow" for permissions). Also fix the Buy Online Pickup In Store description, which incorrectly claimed Multiship was a required dependency — only Store Locator is required.

- #1721 `0a9c054` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Scope the cart's `shopperProducts.getProducts` request to an explicit `expand` list (`availability,bundled_products,images,prices,promotions,variations`) covering only the fields the cart UI consumes. Drops `set_products`, `recommendations`, `links`, `options`, `custom_properties`, and `validation` from the response.

- #1747 `93f81c3` Thanks @seckardt_sfemu! - Scope the mini cart's `shopperProducts.getProducts` request to an explicit `expand` list covering only the fields the mini cart UI consumes (#1747).

- #1724 `aa50839` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Simplify .env.default and decouple E2E baseline overrides

- #1620 `f346864` Thanks @kevin-he_sfemu! - Split `vite.config.ts` into per-plugin files under `vite-plugins/`, and extract checkout chunking into a dedicated `codeSplitting` plugin. Plugin order now puts `codeSplitting` before `storefrontNext` so the SDK's i18n plugin can wrap the user-supplied `manualChunks`.

- #1649 `c48cb99` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Standardize SCAPI requests error handling - Cart Page

- #1633 `5dba180` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Standardize SCAPI requests error handling - Product Detail Page

- #1584 `f34059f` Thanks @j-sheth_sfemu! - Standardize SCAPI requests error handling - Product List Page

- #1718 `19510ea` Thanks @jie-dai_sfemu! - Storybook infra: extract memory-router setup into `.storybook/decorators/`, slim `preview.tsx`, and standardize per-component story mocks

- #1699 `5ee459a` Thanks @alex-vuong_sfemu! - Unify sanitizePrefix and stripPathPrefix into one helper

- #1926 `8f1d9ba` Thanks @daniel-diaz_sfemu! - Rewrite adapter pattern guide to reflect analytics-only scope; fix eventToggles casing in config example (snake_case keys, not camelCase)

- #1825 `67f7c55` Thanks @kumaravinash_sfemu! - Dispatch OTP transparently when SLAS reports an unverified email at the checkout contact step (#1825)

- #1817 `1b5723f` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - PDP variation swatches now activate optimistically on click, eliminating the perceived lag while the variant loader resolves. The selected swatch styling is derived from the in-flight navigation target so the clicked button reflects as active on the next paint, then reconciles cleanly with the canonical URL once the navigation settles. Quick-view and cart-edit modal flows are unaffected — they pass an explicit selection override and continue to bypass URL-driven selection entirely.

- #1675 `0b114f4` Thanks @joel-uong_sfemu! - Reduce SCAPI `productSearch` response payload on PLPs by requesting only the image viewTypes the OOTB product tile reads (`medium` for the hero, `swatch` for color thumbnails) via the `imgTypes` query parameter. Configurable via `search.products.images` — a role-keyed object whose values are derived (`Object.values`) into the SCAPI filter, so adding a new role widens the filter automatically. Set a role to `undefined` to opt out of search filtering for that role.

- #1833 `055af4f` Thanks @kevin-he_sfemu! - Remove unused dependencies: @radix-ui/react-select, zustand, get-port, and stale express 4.x devDependency duplicate

- #1824 `79d68e8` Thanks @jie-dai_sfemu! - Fix three cart-domain Storybook snapshot harnesses that were silently capturing `null` baselines: `cart-quantity-picker`, `cart-item-edit-button`, and `cart-item-modal`. Replaced full-replacement `vi.mock('react-router')` with `importOriginal` partial mocks so `RouterProvider` keeps working and `<Story />` actually renders into the snapshot. Re-recorded the 12 affected snapshots.

- #1824 `79d68e8` Thanks @jie-dai_sfemu! - Normalize the `payment-schedule-modal-content` component-folder layout per Pattern 13. The component lived as a flat `info-modal/renderers/payment-schedule-modal-content.tsx` next to its `payment-schedule-modal-content/stories/` folder; moved it into `payment-schedule-modal-content/index.tsx` so component, stories, and snapshots all live under one folder. Imports unchanged thanks to TypeScript module resolution; only the relative `../types` was retargeted to `../../types` from the deeper file.

- #1794 `4a02487` Thanks @s-hussain_sfemu! - Replace exact inventory counts on the PDP with bucketed status messages — In stock, Few items left, 1 item left, Out of stock — and handle perpetual-quantity items cleanly so they no longer surface a literal unit count

- #1893 `e0139ad` Thanks @alex-vuong_sfemu! - Fix: `getOrCreateWishlist` no longer blocks the loader for ~1.5s on every fresh `customerId`. The POST response from `createCustomerProductList` is now used directly when it carries an `id`, eliminating the hardcoded `setTimeout(1500)` + post-create GET that was previously waiting for index propagation. The sleep + re-fetch remains as a fallback for the rare case where the POST returns a body without `id`, gated by a `warn` log so production telemetry can confirm. Affects every wishlist-mounting route (homepage, cart, PDP, PLP, search, account overview) on first load after SLAS issues a new `gcid`.

- #1796 `542bb24` Thanks @s-hussain_sfemu! - `/wishlist` no longer redirects shoppers with expired sessions to `/login`. Guest shoppers (and registered shoppers whose session is no longer usable) now see the guest wishlist with a persistent sign-in banner so they can recover at their own pace.

## v0.4.0 (May 5, 2026)

- Design layer: Wire `contentLinkUuid` through regions and story fixtures to support content blocks
- **Cart line item:** Restore the edit button for non-standard, non-bonus products alongside the newly added wishlist toggle and remove action.
- Broke down app.css into a more organized system for readability and discoverability #1474
- **Cart line item:** Removed the edit action from the line card, added an inline wishlist add/remove toggle, removed the product description block, and removed the delivery pill so the row focuses on image, title, attributes, price, and quantity.
- Fix promotions always showing as 0 in order summary and order confirmation when only item-level discounts are applied — now includes `productItems[].priceAdjustments` alongside `orderPriceAdjustments` (#1557)
- Remove dead `ssr.noExternal` / `ssr.target` block from `vite.config.ts` — production SSR inlining is handled by the SDK's `managedRuntimeBundlePlugin`, and dev works with Vite's default ESM externalization (#1540)
- Standardize SCAPI requests error handling - Homepage (#1537)
- Add `LoginModal` component with support for password, passwordless, and social login modes (#1501)
- Move locale chunking from `vite.config.ts` into SDK `i18nPlugin`; remove TODO comment
- Add login preferences middleware and context for managing email verification preferences (#1453)
- Remove manual `contentLinkUuid` type extensions in favor of SCAPI types
  - `ComponentType` now uses `contentLinkUuid`, `fragment`, `localized`, `visible` from Shopper Experience API v1.3.0
- Document the use of dynamic images (#1519)
- Update Page Designer middleware and `vite.config.ts` to align with upstream `@salesforce/mrt-utilities` conditional export flow (no local Vite alias requirement) (#1533)
- Standardize behaviors of API errors in Checkout (#1521)
- Migrate i18n infrastructure to SDK: replace `src/lib/i18next.ts`, `src/lib/i18next.client.ts`, and `scripts/aggregate-extension-locales.js` with imports from `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime/i18n` and `sfnext locales aggregate-extensions`
- Fix locale bundle bloat, SSR 404 plain-text response, and homepage links ignoring active locale on error pages
- [UX Fix] Promo code component to match design (#1525)
- Mini cart item UX refresh: update product/price hierarchy, stack quantity controls, and improve long promotion wrapping behavior (#1510)
- Standardize action error handling with semantic error codes: actions return structured `{ code, message }` errors instead of plain strings (#1508)
- Extract Vitest config into dedicated `vitest.config.ts`, inline coverage thresholds (#1518)
- Add support for optional `sh` parameter to dynamic images (#1503)
- [UX Fix] Fix broken radius overriding system, and minor UX changes according to design (#1495)
- Prefix all checkout UITarget targetIds with `sfcc.` (#1500)
- Flatten default `Card` styling (drop default radius/shadow) (#1489)
- Multiship Guest Add Address now supports different addresseses with same name
- Standardize layout with `section-container` utility: consolidate responsive padding, max-width, and centering into a single reusable class (#1483)
- Update checkout CTA text (#1480)
- Update performance-related documentation (#1485, #1486, #1499)
- Ensure `<Link/>`, `<NavLink/>`, and `<useNavigate/>` also rewrite index routes (#1470)
- Prevent unnecessary navigation menu re-renders (#1446)
- My Account: overview "rate recent purchases" card (below recent orders) linking to order details; order details per-line Rate & Review using the PDP write-review modal, with "Review submitted" state after submit
- Update style for Deliver to Multiple Addresses button (#1463)
- Fix re-render cycles on PDP due to shared Suspense boundary (#1434)
- User registration verified badge and spinner
- Update order summary UX
- UX changes on checkout page
- Bug fix to allow Canadian saved shipping address
- My Account: Hide auto-generated address IDs and remove Address Title field; show customer name with Default badge instead
- Add `config:inspect`, `config:push-env`, and `b2c` npm scripts; add `@salesforce/b2c-cli` dev dependency for MRT environment variable management
- Add support for OOTB API Key for Google Address Autocomplete feature in production instances (#1509)
- Remove unused /callback route
- Remove unused Page Designer dev proxy from vite.config.ts (@)
- Rename server-only source files to `.server.ts` so the React Router build plugin enforces the server/client boundary at compile time
- Checkout: Shipping method styling as per UX
- Added SDD (Spec-Driven Development) support with multi-agent code generation
- ProductCarousel: fix category-driven product fetching in Page Designer — loader now correctly invoked when `categoryId` attribute is set
- ProductCarousel: hide empty-state placeholder on live storefront; "Select a product" now only shown in Page Designer design mode
- ProductCarousel: add `categoryId` and `limit` Page Designer attribute definitions; update cartridge metadata
- Fix social login redirect flow and callback handler (#1386)
- Extend `useSite()` to return `{ site, language, locale, currency }` and remove `CurrencyProvider`/`useCurrency()` (#1384)
- Add Cloudflare Turnstile bot protection integration for passwordless login with graceful degradation
- Remove `'use client'` directives from template app source files (#1375)
- Save checkout user info for new user consistently
- Save phone number to `phoneMobile` in addition to `phoneHome` on customer profile update (#1373)
- Calculate basket after OTP verificatiion
- Update accessibility baseline and fix accessibility violations on order list page
- Consolidate `action.set-site`, `action.set-locale`, and `action.set-currency` into a single `action.set-site-context` route (#1342)
- Clean up RSC/React Server Components references from documentation, comments, and config (#1363)
- Remove internal "odyssey" codename references from codebase
- Add template support for registering and calling custom APIs through generated SCAPI clients
- Add configurable navigation menu options `rootCategoryId`, `maxDepth`(#1292)
- Fix Vite dev server warnings for font loading from public directory (#1286)
- Restored Page Designer aspect definitions for PDP and PLP
- Added fallback functionality for Core Region component and added two regions on AboutUs page region(`headline` and `additionalinformation`)
- Handle all Page Designer API errors gracefully in `pageLoader.ts` to prevent dev server crashes
- Add comprehensive checkout E2E tests for registered shopper flows: saved/new payment methods, View All/View Less pagination, save card to profile, shipping address modal (add/edit), non-default address selection, shipping method change, billing address selection, basket persistence across sessions, and Place Order button visibility
- Add SCAPI helper utilities for API-based registered shopper setup (register, login via PKCE, create address, update profile, add payment instrument) to speed up E2E test setup
- Page Designer: `storefrontnext_base` default `@Component` group, Layout/Content groups, resolved region type refs for inclusions/exclusions; updated cartridge metadata and static registry
- Hero Banner: Page Designer **Overlay Position** (nine placements: top/middle/bottom × left/center/right) and **Overlay Alignment** (text/CTA left, center, right); updated cartridge metadata
- Hero Banner: Page Designer **Title Typography**, **Subtitle Typography**, optional **Title/Subtitle Color** (hex), and **Button Style** (Primary/Secondary/Tertiary) for the CTA; hide CTA when link is empty; derive default CTA label from URL; legacy horizontal overlay values map to the nine-position grid; updated cartridge metadata

## v0.3.1 (Apr 13, 2026)

- Fix `pnpm install` failing on freshly generated storefronts: add `trustPolicyExclude` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml.hbs` for `chokidar` and `semver`, which lost their SLSA provenance attestations and triggered `ERR_PNPM_TRUST_DOWNGRADE`
- Add `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` for `@salesforce/storefront-next-dev` and `@salesforce/storefront-next-runtime` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml.hbs` so freshly released SDK versions can be installed without hitting the 48-hour quarantine window
- Fix template CI: `build-bundle` action now falls back to `--no-frozen-lockfile` when no lockfile exists; `deploy.yml` adds missing `SFCC_ACCOUNT_MANAGER_HOST` env var
